name: Fundamentals of Scientific Thinking and Research Methodology
learningOutcomes: Successful completion of the course implies that the students will be able to: · understand the nature of scientific knowledge · understand the main paradigms of science · understand the differences between quantitative and qualitative research methodology · know basics and reflect on research ethics and research materials · know how to use and reflect on the use scientific research methods · know how to frame a study and how to plan and conduct data collection · know well the basics of case study research and the main features of ethnographic, action, focus group and narrative research designs and reflect on the suitability of each method · conduct qualitative content analysis · assess and reflect on the quality of master’s theses · generate a viable research plan
content: The aim of the course is to deepen the understanding of master-level students at LBS of the fundamentals of scientific thinking and research methodology. The more practical aim is to give tools and support their master’s thesis process. In addition to the core principles of scientific research, the course caters a wide range of potential methods and research designs for a master’s thesis. The focus is on qualitative methodology. Please choose the course on quantitative research methods if you wish to write a quantitative master’s thesis.
prerequisites: Bachelor’s thesis and bachelor-level research methodology course.
learningMaterial: Eriksson, P. and Kovalainen, A. (2008 or 2015). Qualitative Methods in Business Research A collection of articles. Additional reading: Silverman, David (2005) "Doing qualitative research: a practical handbook". Hirsjärvi, Sirkka ym. (2009) "Tutki ja kirjoita".
evaluationCriteria: Comparison of scientific paradigms and consideration of biases of thinking 15%, Comparison of three qualitative research methods 15%, Qualitative Content analysis 25%, Analysis of qualitative master’s theses 20%, Research plan for a master’s thesis 25%.
workload: Grading 1-5.
equivalentCoursesInfo: Can't be included into a same degree with A320A4000 Research in International Business and Entrepreneurship.

name: Fuzzy Sets and Fuzzy Logic
searchTags: Written examination in the examination schedule
learningOutcomes: By the end of the course student will be able to - understand basic mathematical concepts related to fuzzy set theory and fuzzy logic - model uncertain concepts using fuzzy set theory - construct fuzzy models - deduce meaningful information from fuzzy models
content: The course consists of basics of fuzzy set theory, algebras of fuzzy sets, fuzzy quantities, logical aspects of fuzzy sets, operations of fuzzy sets, fuzzy relations, aggregation operators, common fuzzy inference systems, including Mamdani's, Larsen's and Tsukamoto inference and Sugeno model.
prerequisites: Bachelor level mathematics courses e.g.: BM20A6700 Matematiikka I,, BM20A6800 Matematiikka II, Experience in programming or using mathematical software required e.g.: BM20A4301 Johdatus tekniseen laskentaan or BM20A5001 Principles of Technical Computing
learningMaterial: Klir, G., Yuan, B.: Fuzzy Sets and Fuzzy Logic. Theory and Applications, Prentice Hall, 1995.Fullér, R.: Introduction to Neuro-Fuzzy Systems, Physica-Verlag, 2000. Ross, T.: Fuzzy Logic with Engineering Applications, Wiley, 2017. Passino, K.M., Yurkovich, S.: Fuzzy control, Addison Wesley, 1998.
evaluationCriteria: 0-5, examination 100 %.
workload: Lectures 14 h, demolecture videos 7 h, exercises 14 h, 1st period. Lectures 14 h, demolecture videos 7 h, exercises 14 h, 2nd period. Independent study 90 h. Written examination. Total workload 160 h.

name: Information Systems in Corporate Management and Decision-making
learningOutcomes: The aim of the course is to give extensive general knowledge about corporate information systems and how they are used in corporate decision-making, business control, and as a driver of business development. After the course the students: have an understanding of the corporate information systems stack and the most common types of corporate information systems and where they are used, are able to view a business as a system and its parts as parts of a system, know how information systems can collect, summarize, and analyze corporate information, understand what the practice of fact based management is based on and how it is connected to information systems, know the concept of intelligent systems, know selected methods and tools, understand the types of results that they can provide, and the importance of such results for, for example, making the business more effective through optimization, can identify and critically analyze situations, where information systems can be used to develop business practices.
content: Core content: corporate information stack, business intelligence, big data, Additional content : controlling in a modern corporation based on IS, intelligent systems in business process development, concepts of optimization, machine learning, neural networks, simulation, and cognitive technologies Special content: importance of visualizing knowledge
prerequisites: For master's level students only
learningMaterial: Lecture slides, lecture videos, assigned video material, assigned reading, collection of articles. All materials will be available via Moodle.
evaluationCriteria: Grade 0-5, evaluation 0-100 points, after passed exam extra points from quizzes counted towards the grade, Exam 100%.
workload: Lectures 20 h (available as videos), independent reading assignments (articles), and preparation for lectures 55 h. Quizzes, preparation for the quizzes and the exam 85 h. Total workload for the student 160 h.

name: International Corporate Governance and Financial Reporting
searchTags: Written examination in the examination schedule
learningOutcomes: The course provides an understanding on financial reporting ties with corporate governance and economic performance. Analytical framework of financial reporting and corporate performance are presented thru the needs and effects of corporate governance including the concepts of stakeholder and shareholder. More precisely the effects of ownership, dominant vs minority shareholders, corporate control and managerial compensation are presented. After completing the course, students can critically analyze different aspects of corporate governance and financial reporting, along with their potential effects on corporate performance. Additionally, students will apply theoretical knowledge to practical tasks, enhancing their ability to solve real-world problems related to corporate governance and financial reporting.
content: Corporate governance, financial reporting, firm performance, agency theory, boards, management compensation.
learningMaterial: Goergen, M. (2012). International Corporate Governance, 5th Edition, Pearson. Pratt, Jamie (2011). Financial Accounting in an Economic Context, International Student Version, 8th Edition, Wiley.
evaluationCriteria: Grade 0-5, evaluation 0-100 points, written exam 75 %, in-class excercises 35 %.
workload: Video lectures 9 h. In-class lectures and excercises 8h Independent study and preparation for exam 143 h. Written examination. Total workload 160 h.

name: Internationalization of the Firm and Global Marketing
learningOutcomes: After completing the course, the student will be able to: - understand and evaluate benefits and costs of internationalization of the firm - justify and recommend how to enhance international competitiveness of the firm - analyze and justify the key management decisions related to internationalization of the firm: whether to internationalize, which markets to target, and how to enter selected markets - apply relevant theories and frameworks to explain and facilitate internationalization of particular firms Additionally, the students will develop the following soft transferable skills: - working effectively in a team to achieve goals - showing initiative and leadership abilities - managing and prioritizing one's workload and time effectively - communicating effectively in written and verbal forms
content: - Must know: internationalization motives and barriers; chain of strategic decisions related to internationalization of the firm; risks assessment in international markets; internationalization theories (OLI, Uppsala model, Network approach, Born Global); firm's international competitiveness; international market selection process; factors influencing entry mode choice; characteristics of various entry modes (export modes, intermediate entry modes, hierarchical modes); transaction cost analysis. - Should know: concept of the value chain in internationalization; comparison of SMEs and LSEs in internationalization; global market research; sustainability in internationalization of the firm; the integration-responsiveness framework; organizing strategies - Nice to know: principles of decision-making; functional strategies of an international firm
prerequisites: Sufficient prior business studies and basic knowledge of international business and marketing required.
learningMaterial: - Hollensen, S. (2025) Global Marketing, 9th edition, Pearson Education (older editions apply as well) - Collinson, Narula, Rugman (2024) - International Business, 9th edition, Pearson Education (older editions apply as well) - Cavusgil, Knight Reisenberger (2024) - International Business: the new realities, 6th edition, Pearson - Van Tulder, Van Mil (2023) - Principles of Sustainable Business Frameworks for Corporate Action on the SDGs, 1st edition, Routledge - Additional reading and material to be assigned in class and in Moodle.
evaluationCriteria: 0 - 5. Exam 20 %, individual assignments 15 %, groupwork assignments 30 %, group term paper report 20 %, term paper presentation 10%, peer evaluation report 5 %. Each of the components has to be passed acceptably.
workload: 15 h of lectures, 15 h of seminars, 12 h individual assignments, 40 h groupwork assignments, 40 h group term paper report and presentation, 3 h peer evaluation report, 35 h independent study and preparation for lectures and examination quiz. Total workload 160 h.

name: International Marketing of High Technology Products and Innovations
learningOutcomes: Distinguish the special characteristics of high technology marketing environment (like the type of innovation, market and technology uncertainties, network externalities) and assess external high technology environments (e.g. relating to competitive landscape, consumer behavior, markets) in global scale. Evaluate and justify marketing strategies in high technology environments. Make marketing decisions in high technology environments. Course aims to provide a deep understanding of the functions of marketing regarding challenges and opportunities in high technology products and markets, assist the participants to understand the virtue and limitations of traditional marketing thinking and tools in emergent high technology markets.
content: - Strategy and corporate culture in high tech firms. - Partnerships and alliances. - Marketing research in high tech markets. - Understanding high tech customers. - Product development and management issues in high tech markets. -Distribution channels in high tech markets. - Pricing considerations in high tech markets. - Advertising and promotion in high tech markets. - Introduction to new technologies such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, and blockchain
prerequisites: For summer school students: previous studies in business recommended. For MIMM degree students at LUT: Internationalisation of the Firm and Global Marketing, Strategic Global Marketing Management
learningMaterial: Mohr, Jakki, Sanjit Sengupta, and Stanley Slater (2010) Marketing of High-Technology Products and Innovations. Third Edition. Pearson Prentice Hall. Web site http://marketinghightech.net - Assigned reading
evaluationCriteria: Final grade 0-5. Evaluation 0-100 points:- Exam 50 points- In-class assignments 30 points- Class participation 20 points
workload: - Lectures and in-class assignments 30 hours- Preparing for lectures 25 hours - Preparing for exam 25 hours. Total workload 80 hours..

name: International Market Research and Target Market Selection
learningOutcomes: The course aims to provide the students with the knowledge of the processes related to international market research and target market selection both from theoretical and practical standpoints. The main objectives of the course are: 1) to inspire students with the vision inherent in SME internation-alisation, and demonstrate how to do target market selection, 2) to increase their awareness of the frameworks, tools and techniques used in international target market selection and market research, and also challenges and obstacles integral with interna-tional expansion planning, 3) to equip students with the insights, tools, frameworks, and skills necessary to international target market selection and subse-quent market entry, and 4) to give students knowledge on how to prepare an international market research project.
content: The course unit builds on the foundations of the international business and marketing strategy and focuses on strategies and practices of international target market selection – and market research activities, which provide information for decision making on market entry and target market selection. The course blends informative lectures with case studies and hands-on secondary market research exercises. The core topics are as follows: international market selection and the planning situation in the firm, analysis of international market envi-ronment, market analysis and understanding of customer needs and wants, competitor and environment analyses, the roles of culture and geography in international market research, segmentation, targeting and positioning, information needs and how to conduct basic second-ary and primary market research, sources of information and their use, international market research organization, preliminary choice of target country and market segment (systematic vs. non-systematic, reactive approach), International market selection and its linkages to other parts of the international business strategy. The emphasis will be on the first-time market entry and international-izing SME examples will be used. From that perspective we will: 1) Explore, how to set up objectives for international market re-search and gain an understanding of the data needs. We will use exemplary cases to discuss the problems and opportuni-ties related to international target market selection. 2) Discuss on ‘target market selection’ approaches (systematic vs. non-systematic, reactive approach) and possible data sources and types. 3) Conduct primary and secondary market research activity pro-ject to find information about a specific case. What are the issues which need primary market research activities?
prerequisites: Previous courses in basic marketing (e.g. Principles of Marketing, Marketing Management, Essentials of Marketing) or international business (e.g. Introduction to International Business or International Business Strategy)
learningMaterial: Case studies, slide decks, and template for Market Research Plan will be provided. The additional reading materials from academic and business press articles (i.e. magazine, newspaper, and journal arti-cles) will be distributed through the class time prior to the class dis-cussion. Suggested textbooks: Hollensen, Svend (2017) Global Marketing (7th ed.). Pearson. ISBN-13: 978-1292100111 Craig, C. S., & Douglas, S. P. (2005). International marketing re-search. Chichester: John Wiley & Sons.
evaluationCriteria: Final grade 0-5. Evaluation 0-100 points: - Attendance / Class activity 10% - Active participation in team working activities / in-class case pro-jects 40% - Market research plan/project (individual assignment conducted af-ter the in-class days) 50%
workload: - Lectures and in-class assignments 30 hours - Preparing for lectures/in class- sessions 20 hours - Market research plan / project 30 hours Total workload 80 hours.

name: Introduction to Business and Culture in Finland
learningOutcomes: After completing the course, students will be able to: - understand Finland as a context for doing business - recognize and critically examine the role of Finland in global markets - appreciate Finnish culture in general and business culture in particular - analyze challenges and opportunities of doing business in and with Finland - discover, evaluate and create international business opportunities between Finland and other countries
content: Finland as a business context; Finland as a cultural context; Finland in international business; International business and entrepreneurial opportunities, Entrepreneurial Ecosystems and start-up scene in Finland
evaluationCriteria: Accepted/Failed. All course assignments (four individual reflective essays and a group term paper) shall be passed in order to complete the course. There is no exam in the course.
workload: 21 hours of lectures; 8 hours of seminars; 35 hours of term paper preparation; 16 hours reflection essays. Total 80 hours.

name: Introduction to Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability
learningOutcomes: This course aims to familiarize the students with the basics of corporate social responsibility (CSR) and sustainability, including common critiques of these concepts as well as their potential to achieve positive change. During the course, students will actively learn about and reflect on various sustainability issues and topics affecting businesses operating in a global environment, and possible ways for companies to address these issues through CSR and sustainability strategies, practices and interactions with stakeholders. Guest lectures and class exercises give the students an opportunity to apply their knowledge to actual business practice. Finally, students can improve their professional skills (e.g. communication and interaction skills) during the course through class discussions and group assignments. Upon completion of the course, students should be able to: 1) Understand and critically examine key concepts and frameworks related to CSR and sustainability. 2) Recognize and assess various environmental, social, economic and ethical issues caused by, and affecting, companies operating in a global context. 3) Distinguish and analyse various types of CSR and sustainability strategies, practices and other ways of addressing sustainability issues. 4) Apply theoretical frameworks and research findings related to CSR and sustainability to real-life phenomena and business practice. 5) Produce CSR and sustainability-related texts and materials.
content: CSR and sustainability frameworks and concepts, environmental, social, economic, and ethical issues, CSR and sustainability strategy, CSR and sustainability practice, activism, reputation, corporate crises, communications, governance, digitalization, globalization, supply chain sustainability, sustainable investing, and cross-sector interactions.
learningMaterial: Rasche, A., Morsing, M., & Moon, J. (Eds.). (2017). Corporate Social Responsibility: Strategy, Communication, Governance. Cambridge University Press: Cambridge. Lecture slides and materials. Additional readings, videos and course materials announced in the syllabus and/or distributed during lectures.
evaluationCriteria: Grade 0-5. Evaluation (0-100 points) is based on final paper exam (100 %). All assignments and the exam must be passed to complete the course.
workload: Lectures and guest lectures (16h), preparation for lectures and class discussions (54h), and independent study for the final exam (90h). Total workload: 160h. The course requires advance preparation for the lectures, active participation in class discussions, successful completion of all assignments, and independent study.

name: Introduction to International Business and Planning
learningOutcomes: To familiarize the students with the fundamentals of international business in general and strategic planning for international business in particular. To provide the students with the analytical skills required for critical evaluation of actual international business strategies.
content: - The changes in the international business environment and their effect on strategic planning. - Theories of international trade and business. - The institutions of international trade and business. - The essence of competitive strategy. - Levels of strategic planning. - International expansion strategy. - Supporting research. - International marketing strategy: entry modes, targeting, product, service, pricing, promotion, sales and CRM. - International functional strategies. - Case studies.
prerequisites: Basic course in marketing
learningMaterial: The study material will be distributed at the beginning of the lectures.
evaluationCriteria: Graded 0-5 on the basis of case studies and class participation 20 % and written examination 80 %, evaluation 0 – 100 points. 50 % class attendance and participation required.
workload: Intensive course during 1. period. 35 hours of lectures, interactive analyses, case exercises and assignments, carried out by the student 65 hours, preparation for the written exam and written examination 60 h. Total course 160 h.

name: Introduction to International Marketing and Purchasing
learningOutcomes: The aim of the course is to develop students' capabilities and understanding of the basics and strategies of marketing and purchasing in an international context, including sustainability aspects. The students will gain an understanding of the connections between marketing and procurement in company operations and are able to analyze the characteristics of the international business environment and different cultures in marketing and procurement management. After completing the course, students should be able to: 1. understand and apply knowledge to management of marketing and purchasing issues in international environment 2. analyze the characteristics of international and intercultural marketing and purchasing 3. design purchasing strategies and use marketing mix tools in international context 4. comprehend sustainability considerations in marketing and purchasing 5. collaborate in teams to facilitate communication, engage in discussions, and collectively reach group decisions
content: Opportunities and challenges in international marketing and purchasing operations. The interconnectedness of marketing and purchasing in a company’s operations. Sustainability considerations in marketing and procurement management in international context. Marketing mix tools and purchasing strategy development tools.
learningMaterial: Lecture materials, other course material will be announced in the beginning of the course.
evaluationCriteria: Grade 0 – 5, evaluation 0-100 points. Group project 30 %, case study in groups 20 %, continuous individual evaluation 50 %. All assignments must be passed to obtain the final grade.
workload: Interactive lectures 14 h. Group seminars 8 h. Company project from a given topic and case assignment as a teamwork. Obligatory presentation of the company project in seminar. Written project report and powerpoint slides. Written report from the case assignment. Individual assignment, reflection of the groupworks or a learning diary. Attendance and preparation for interactive lectures 28 h, Group seminar presentation preparation and attendance 22 h, Case study 10 h, Groupwork preparation 60 h, Individual assignment preparation 40 h. Continuous assessment. Total workload 160 h.

name: Bachelor's Thesis, Business Administration
learningOutcomes: After the completion of the course, the student knows the basic principles of doing business economics research and of research methodologies employed in it. He/she can independently write the B.Sc. thesis that relies on the theoretical framework and includes also an empirical part. Students can search for and choose relevant literature and analyze the empirical material. The student can also report the main findings of his/her thesis and give an oral presentation of them. Moreover, he/she can assess and discuss project reports written by other students. The student is also capable of defending his/her own B.Sc. thesis in a seminar session.
content: The basics of the research work, information sources and services of the library, the basics of academic writing. Applying of research methods relative to empirical data. The argumentation and commentary of other student's thesis.
prerequisites: All general studies of Bachelor's degree, A130A0350 Kvantitatiiviset tutkimusmenetelmät ja A130A0400 Laadulliset tutkimusmenetelmät and at least half of the intermediate specialization studies completed.
learningMaterial: 1.) Hirsjärvi, S., Remes, P., Sajavaara, P.: Tutki ja kirjoita, 2001 or newer. 2.) Koskinen, I., Alasuutari, P., Peltonen, T.: Laadulliset menetelmät kauppatieteissä, 2005. 3.) Other assigned reading.
evaluationCriteria: Numerical assessment (0-5). Bachelor’s thesis 91%, presentation and discussion 9%.
workload: Seminars and independent work during periods 1 and 2 OR 3 and 4. Two alternative groups, one starting in the 1st period and the other in the 3rd period. Total workload 260 h.

name: Basic Course in Financial Accounting
learningOutcomes: The aim of the course is to give basic skills to prepare and understand bookkeeping and financial statements. After completion of the course students: - understand the role of accounting as a part of business and planning - can definitions and purposes of accounting - can basic regulation and principles of accounting - can basic content and purpose of financial statement and accounting policies and principles - recognize the basic principles of VAT - recognize the basic principles of income taxation in limited company General aim of the course is to improve following personal skills of the students: - problem solving
content: Basic concepts and utilization of financial accounting. Posting entries of focal transactions of business bookkeeping and foaming of financial statement. Basic principles and regulation of business bookkeeping. Basic principles of VAT and business income taxation.
learningMaterial: 1) Recorded lectures, exercise material and recorded exercise solutions in Moodle. 2) Ihantola, Eeva-Mari ; Leppänen, Pasi. Yrityksen kirjanpito. Liiketapahtumista tilinpäätökseen. 2023 or newer. As an eBook at LUT Academic Library.
evaluationCriteria: Grade 0-5, evaluation 0-100 points, Examination in Exam 100%
workload: Starting lecture 2 h, 2nd period. Recorded lectures totally 16 h. Independent exercises with recorded solutions 80 h. Exam and preparation for exam 62 h. During the study year will be organized 4 Examination in Exams with a pre-information event. Total workload 160 h.

name: Basics in Accounting
learningOutcomes: After completing the course, the student will be able to use accounting methods to support business decision-making and planning. The student will have basic skills to analyze financial information and utilize it across different business areas of a company.
content: Course topics: The importance of accounting in businesses and society Fields of accounting: Key concepts of management accounting and financial accounting Financial accounting: Key statements and their analysis Management accounting methods and their application in business operations Financial planning and forecasting
learningMaterial: Lecture notes and the following recommended books: Ikäheimo, S., Malmi, T. & Walden, R. (2016 or newer): Yrityksen laskentatoimi. Also available as an e-book. Jormakka, R., Koivusalo, K., Lappalainen, J., & Niskanen, M. (2021 or newer): Laskentatoimi. Also available as an e-book. Neilimo, K. & Uusi-Rauva, E. (2014 or newer): Johdon laskentatoimi.
evaluationCriteria: Grade 0-5. The Exam-electronic examination accounts for 100% of the grade.
workload: Lectures 14 h, individual assignments/independent work 20 h, exam preparation 44 h, Exam 2 h. Total workload 80 h.

name: Research in Accounting
learningOutcomes: During the course, the students will deepen their knowledge on accounting research. Upon completion of the course the students are: - Familiar with the key research traditions and practices in management accounting and financial accounting; - Able to assess different kind of research methods and data and their applicability; - Knowledgeable about the current themes in accounting field and key international refereed accounting journals; - Able to discuss research results both from the theoretical and empirical perspectives; - Familiar with good scientific practice; and - Able to utilize the knowledge in doing one's own research.
content: Research traditions in accounting, key theories and current themes. Familiarizing oneself with a typical research process, methods and potential datasets.
prerequisites: Accounting/Financial Management Bachelor's level studies.
learningMaterial: 1. Lecture notes. 2. Journal articles. 3. Other assigned reading.
evaluationCriteria: Grade 0-5, evaluation 0-100 points. Conducting and presenting literature review 45%, conducting and presenting empirical research and giving peer feedback 50%, independent assignment 5% (no exam). All assignments must be passed to obtain final grade.
workload: Lectures 4h, coaching sessions 4h, seminars 8h, conducting literature review and empirical research within groups 140h, independent assignment 4h. Total workload 160h.

name: Master's Thesis, International Business and Entrepreneurship
learningOutcomes: The overall goal of the thesis is for the student to display the knowledge and capability required for independent work as a Master of Science in Economics and Business Administration, and especially in the area of international business and entrepreneurship. After completing the thesis, students will be able to carry out independently a scientific research project and will thus be able to: - delimit and define the purpose and the topic of the research - have a deep understanding on the theory, current research and research methods relevant to their main subject - design and apply theoretical frameworks in own research and in solving empirical research problems - independently identify and formulate research problems and to plan and, by using appropriate methods, carry out advanced tasks within specified time limits - integrate knowledge and to analyze, assess and deal with complex phenomena, issues and situations - report scientific research in written academic format, clearly present and discuss conclusions and the knowledge and arguments behind them.
content: The student applies the knowledge and skills of previous studies and attends the Master's Thesis Seminars covering the specific features of a scientific research process and related requirements.
prerequisites: Thesis project idea that has been preliminary approved by the thesis supervisor (submitted in Moodle). Approximately 30 ECTS cr. MIBE studies.
learningMaterial: Master's Thesis - instructions, seminar materials available in Moodle and Uni portals.
evaluationCriteria: Thesis grade 1-5, Master's Thesis seminar: pass/fail. All theses submitted for evaluation will undergo similarity check for plagiarism.
workload: You can enroll the course and start your thesis work throughout the academic year. Online seminars are run several times, and you can choose which ones you participate (timings confirmed in Moodle). If you do not finish your thesis during the same academic year you enroll again the next year. Hence you can enroll already during the first year of your masters programme, but supervisor for your thesis is only assigned to you after completion of thesis idea paper assignment. Active participation in seminars, successful completion of the required seminar assignments on topic selection, literature review, research aim, research questions and theoretical framework, presentation of the research plan, acting as discussants for other's work, writing of the thesis and completing the final version of the Thesis under supervision of assigned Master's Thesis supervisors. Total workload consisting of research seminars, seminar assignments, research execution and written reporting 800 h.

name: Master's Thesis, Strategy, Innovation and Sustainability
learningOutcomes: Upon completion of the course, students should be able to carry out a research project independently and to report the research in written format according to scientific practices, and will thus be able to: - delimit and define the purpose and the topic of the research - have a deep understanding on the theory, current research and research methods relevant to their main subject - design and apply theoretical frameworks in own research and in solving empirical research problems - independently identify and formulate issues and to plan and, by using appropriate methods, carry out advanced tasks within specified time limits - integrate knowledge and to analyze, assess and deal with complex phenomena, issues and situations - report scientific research in written academic format, clearly present and discuss conclusions, and the knowledge and arguments behind them
content: The Master Thesis Seminar aims to support MSIS students through the process of writing a Master thesis. The student applies the knowledge and skills of previous studies and attends the Master's Thesis Seminars covering the specific features of a scientific research process and related requirements.

name: Multivariate and Econometric Methods for Doctoral Students
learningOutcomes: The aim of the course is to give extensive general knowledge about the main econometric and multivariate analysis methods. After completion of the course students: - understand the role of multivariate analysis in scientific research - can evaluate and compare the applicability of various multivariate methods - are able to collect numerical data from databases commonly applied in business research - can apply multivariate analysis methods for cross-sectional and panel data - can conduct the analyses with Stata software - can interpret and evaluate the results of the analyses - can report the results according to good scientific practice
content: Measure development and factor analysis, linear regression, analyses of variance, logistic regression, panel data regression. Use of Stata software, use of international databases of statistical data.
prerequisites: Basic courses in statistics and economics.
learningMaterial: Hair, Joseph Jr. et al.: Multivariate data analysis. Prentice Hall, 1998. Hill, R.C. - Griffiths, W.E. - Judge, G.G.: Undergraduate Econometrics, 2nd edition, 2001 or newer edition: Hill, R.C. - Griffiths, W.E. - Lim, G.C.: Principles of Econometrics, 3rd or 4th edition, 2008 or 2012.
evaluationCriteria: Final grade accepted vs. failed, based on the written report.
workload: Video lectures 20 h, independent exercises 20 h, independent data collection and analysis using the Stata software, writing of report 120 h. Total workload for student 160 h. Students can enroll to the course and complete it any time during the academic year.
equivalentCoursesInfo: If you have already completed the course A350A0250 Multivariate and Econometric Analysis Methods, you can't select this course.

name: Sales Process and Customer Relationship Development
learningOutcomes: After completing the course, the student: is able to build and analyze different stages of the sales process and understands their role in the company's business model. can develop effective and scalable sales processes that support the company's strategic goals and various customer relationships. understands the role of technologies and analytics in a data-driven sales process. understands the importance of collaboration with marketing and other company functions as part of the sales process implementation.
content: Sales processes as part of the company's strategy and business model. The stages of the sales process, their optimization, and adaptation to different contexts. Customer value and the customer journey perspective in sales process design. The role of technologies, analytics, and metrics in developing a data-driven sales process. Collaboration between sales, marketing, and other business functions. Customer relationship development and the creation of upselling and cross-selling opportunities.
evaluationCriteria: Video reflections 15 %, blog and participation in Moodle discussions 35 %, pair assignment 50 %. Grading scale 0-5.
workload: Lectures 12 h, video reflections 9 h, literature review, blog writing, and participation in discussions on Moodle 44 h, pair assignment 95 h. Total workload 160 hours.

name: Perspectives on financial reporting and auditing
learningOutcomes: After completing the course, students will - understand the essential and current issues regarding financial reporting and auditing in practice, - be able to apply this knowledge in practical work life, - understand and be able to apply research-based knowledge in analyzing financial reporting and auditing issues, and - be able to apply research-based knowledge in developing their own professionalism. A general objective of the course is to improve the students' team work and problem-solving skills as well as the organization and time management skills.
content: Key themes of the course: - Current topics, changes and specific issues in financial management and auditing - Digitalization and emerging technologies in financial reporting and auditing - Sustainability reporting and its assurance - Reliability of financial reporting - Scientific research related to current issues Company cooperation: Visiting lecturers will provide current and practical perspectives on the key topics. Use of AI applications: In this course, the responsible and ethical use of AI is approved according to the LUT guidance on the right use of AI applications. The use of AI must be reported.
prerequisites: B.Sc. studies in accounting/financial management
learningMaterial: Articles, lecture material, other material announced by the lecturer
evaluationCriteria: Grade 0-5, evaluation 0-100 points, learning assignments 60 %, written essay in groups 40 %. All parts of the course have to be performed and accepted to get a final grade.
workload: Online lectures 12 h, seminars 6 h, written essay in groups 54 h, self-employed working and learning assingments 88 h. Total workload 160 h.
equivalentCoursesInfo: Replaces the course A210A0460 Tilinpäätösraportoinnin teemoja, and can not be included in the same degree.

name: Optimization in Business and Industry
searchTags: Written examination in the examination schedule
learningOutcomes: By the end of the course student will be able to - select/ employ mathematical models for various optimization problems - use optimization software - interpret information from optimization results - understand the basic principles of different optimization algorithms for linear, mixed-integer linear, and nonlinear optimization
content: Formulation of optimization models. Linear programming and mixed-integer linear programming, nonlinear optimization algorithms. Solving optimization problems using Matlab Optimization Toolbox. Business and industry oriented practical examples, i.e. factory, warehouse, sales allocation models etc.
prerequisites: Experience in programming or using mathematical software required.BM20A4301 Johdatus tekniseen laskentaan or BM20A5001 Principles of Technical Computing.
learningMaterial: Taha, H.A.: Operations Research an introduction, 8th edition, Pearson/Prentice-Hall, 2007. Hillier, F.S., Lieberman, G.J.: Introduction to Operations Research, 8th edition, McGraw-Hill, 2004.
evaluationCriteria: 0-5, examination 100 %
workload: Lectures 28 h, exercises 28 h, 4th period. Independent study 74 h, practical assignment 30 h. Written examination. Total workload 160 h.

name: Principles of Management and Leadership
learningOutcomes: The course empowers students with the skills to make meaningful changes in the world by leading and managing organizations. Students will learn to demonstrate an understanding of management functions: planning, organizing, leading, and controlling, as well as leadership styles, to describe and apply concepts, theories, and practices relevant to exercising management and leadership in modern organizations, to demonstrate ethical, sustainable, and socially responsible decision-making and management practices, collectively map organizational management and leadership challenges, and co-create solutions to manage these challenges effectively and efficiently.
content: The course focuses on planning, organizing, leading, and controlling, management theories, managerial roles, and leadership styles. The topics are discussed in a global context – global economy, free trade, sustainable business, and global south-north differences – requiring an ethical and sustainable approach to management and leadership. The course is highly interactive, connecting theory and practice through inviting industry guests as well as a team workshop carried out by an external lecturer.
prerequisites: none
learningMaterial: Kinicki, A., & Williams, B. K. (2024). Management: A practical introduction. McGraw-Hill. Lecture slides Additional materials: in class and Moodle
evaluationCriteria: Students will be evaluated on a personal learning diary (40%) and group assignment (40%). Lecture attendance will be credited (20%). Each of the components has to be passed acceptably.
workload: This course is conducted in a contact teaching mode, requiring significant investment of time outside of the lecture hall. In-class hours (27 hours): 27 hours of lectures and workshops. Out-class hours (133 hours): preparation for lectures and workshops 13 hours. Collaboration for the course group work is 70 hours; writing a learning diary is 50 hours. Total 160 h.

name: Master's Thesis, Accounting
learningOutcomes: The overall goal of the thesis is for the student to display the knowledge and capability required for an independent work as a Master of Science in Economics and Business Administration, and especially in the area of accounting. After completing the thesis, students will be able to carry out independently a scientific research project and thus will be able to: - delimit and define the purpose and the topic of the research; - display a deep understanding on the theory, current research and research methods relevant to their main subject; - design and apply theoretical frameworks in one’s own research and in solving empirical research problems; - identify and formulate issues and collect and analyze empirical research material by using appropriate methods; - clearly present and report the research results, and discuss the conclusions and their implications in the light of previous academic work; - report scientific research in written academic format.
content: The student applies the knowledge and skills of previous studies and actively attends the thesis seminars covering the specific features of a scientific research process and related requirements.
prerequisites: Approximately 30 ECTS cr. of Accounting master's studies.
learningMaterial: Master's Thesis instructions, lecture notes and other assigned reading.
evaluationCriteria: Thesis grade 1-5, Master's Thesis seminar: pass/fail. All theses submitted for evaluation will undergo similarity check for plagiarism.
workload: Seminar work throughout the academic year. Rolling enrollment throughout the academic year. Active participation in research seminars and successful completion of the required seminar assignments, including topic selection, research plan, collecting research data and conducting the research, presenting the thesis and acting as a discussant for other’s work in a thesis seminar, writing and completing the final version of the Master’s thesis. The seminar includes joint research seminars and meetings with the supervisors. Total workload 810h.

name: Prototype Project at J. Hyneman Center
learningOutcomes: 1. to know the basic concepts in prototype production, e.g. perspectives of generation and iteration 2. to know the role of customer value and user experience in prototype production 3. to understand the role of prototype production in the wholeness of an innovation process 4. to understand the role of prototype production as a part of expertise service 5. to have knowledge about different kinds of requirements of prototype production as teamwork and collaboration 6. to have knowledge about prototyping and different types of prototyping activities 7. to know the key concepts and terms used in evaluation 8. to have knowledge of different types of evaluation criteria for prototypes and prototype production methods 9. to analyze the role and importance of the prototype in the real-life context of being eventually in production. 10. to be able to plan and execute a prototype project in a given time-line 11. to be able to collaborate in teams 12. to be able to propose a solution and recommendations for next steps in prototype testing and decision making.
content: The course is based on a prototype project at J. Hyneman Center (JHC). The project is carried out mostly independently at JHC. The original initiative for the prototype building can come from students or from an outside organization. With a high demand of self-organization and independency, the course is at advanced level. The course applies problem-based learning to a concrete prototype development task. Students may work in appropriate size multidiscipline groups. Each group will work mostly independently and self-organizing way, and their learning objectives will be tailored on the basis of their targets in the beginning the course. The course contains of determining the actual problem or target, the acquisition of needed knowledge and skills, determination, comparison and selection of possible different process alternatives, sketching and designing the manufacturing process, selecting needed materials and equipment, economic calculations in an appropriate level and building & testing the prototype. The learning during the course will be presented e.g. via portfolio or reflective and comprehensive report, and presenting the results to an audience e.g. in a seminar or conference.
learningMaterial: Selected by project cases.
evaluationCriteria: Grade 0-5. Evaluation is based on the course assessment tool, available in course Moodle.
workload: Prototype project and portfolio 130 h, report writing and presentation 20 h, reflection 10 h. Total workload 160 h.

name: Real Options and Managerial Decision Making
learningOutcomes: The aim of the course is to give students know-how about how to use, the real options approach as a part of decision making in companies, and how to apply real options thinking in valuation and analysis. After the course the students: - know the mathematical foundations of real options and the connections between the real options approach and financial theory - know the research tradition of real options and are able to critically evaluate the limits of the approach - understand and are able to critically analyze the role of uncertainty and risk in decision-making - are able to apply the real options approach in managerial decision-making situations, and to determine whether real option analysis is suitable/needed for selected problem - know the main model types used in real option valuation and know when each model type can and should be used - have the ability to perform real option valuation with the fuzzy pay-off method and to construct tools for real options valuation with the method
content: Core content: real options vs. financial options, modeling the real options and the limits of modeling, the usability of real options in strategic decision-making Additional content :the use of mathematical tools applied in the real options context Special content: how to use the real options approach in managerial decision-making situations exemplified by means of different real cases, project of constructing a simple real option valuation tool with MS Excel or with Matlab.
prerequisites: For master's program students only
learningMaterial: Lecture slides, Assigned collection of articles, supporting video materials. Materials will be available in Moodle (except for the course book). Collan, M., 2012, The Pay-Off Method: Re-Inventing Investment Analysis – With numerical application examples from different industries, CreateSpace, Charleston, SC, USA (ISBN 978-14-782-3842-3)
evaluationCriteria: Grade 0-5, evaluation 0-100 points. The evaluation will be based on an individual assignment(30%), a group project (30%) and a moodle test (40%)
workload: Lectures, independent readings and preparation for the test 70 h. Individual Assignment and preparation for the group project 90 h. Total workload for the student 160 h.

name: Sales and Marketing Communication
learningOutcomes: After completing the course the student will understand changes in the field of commerce, including buying behavior, marketing communication (MC) and sales management (SM). Student is able to create and design marketing and sales funnel that applies new, more productive technologies. This course will pay special emphasis on understanding the linkages between marketing communication and sales, and the challenges in their integrated management. The learning outcomes of the course are the following: - to understand the evolution of buying behavior, marketing and sales in the era of digital technologies - to understand the role of MC and SM in marketing strategy - to assess the usability of different forms of communication with regard to buyer behavior - to be able to design, implement and manage marketing communication and sales as part of the marketing process - to assess the challenges of integrating MC and sales strategies, and combining traditional tools with new technologies - to evaluate the effectiveness of MC and sales in the changing business environment.
content: Core contents: - The evolution of buying behavior, marketing and sales in the era of digital technologies. - The role of marketing communication (MC) and sales in marketing strategy. - The role of buyer behavior and its effects on the nature of communication (mass vs interactive/personal). - MC and sales process, message and media strategy. - Strategic planning process of MC and sales, challenges of integrating MC and sales management strategies. Additional knowledge: - Sustainability in MC context. Special knowledge: - Digitalization of MC and sales.
prerequisites: A130A0010 Markkinoinnin perusteet (or basic course in marketing). (edit. 19.6.2019)
learningMaterial: Lectures, selected articles, material provided during the course.
evaluationCriteria: Final grade 0-5, evaluation 0-100 points. Exercises 40 points, exam 60 points.
workload: Combined lectures (videos and in-class) and exercises 28 h 2. period. Preparation for exercises 63 h (including written work) and preparation for the exam 71h. Written exam.Total workload for student 160 h.

name: Services Marketing and Customer Experience Management
learningOutcomes: The aim of the course is to provide the students with the knowledge of most central issues of services marketing and customer experience management. After completion of the course the students are able to: - Identify the key concepts and issues related to services marketing and how the nature of services affects marketing activities - Demonstrate how services can be designed according to the needs of customers - Plan service blueprints and understand services marketing from a holistic viewpoint, including the background work and processes that are needed to create and deliver an experience to the customer - Analyze and audit existing services marketing processes by using the principles of service design
content: Foundations for services marketing (e.g. nature of services, services marketing mix, service design). Understanding customers and customer journey. Aligning service design and standards, service quality. Delivering and performing service, managing service promises.
prerequisites: A130A0010 Markkinoinnin perusteet or equivalent basic marketing course.
learningMaterial: Zeithaml, V.A., Bitner, M.J., Gremler, D.D. (2018) Services Marketing: Integrating Customer Focus Across the Firm with Connect Access.(7th ed.). New York: NY. McGraw-Hill Education.Textbook: ISBN: 978-1260051988Other readings and assignments announced before / in the class
evaluationCriteria: Grade 0-5, evaluation 0-100 points: Group assignment 40 points, Learning reports 60 points.
workload: Lectures 14 h, group assignment 34 h, preparing for lectures and writing learning reports 32 h. Total workload for student 80 h.

name: Strategic Management Accounting
learningOutcomes: The aim of the course is to provide an extensive overview of strategic management accounting. Upon completion of the course, the student: - understands how financial management methods support the management process of an organization and help to achieve competitive advantage; - can apply strategic management accounting and cost management approaches in different decision-making and managerial situations; - can make calculations concerning the product and customer profitability and interpret the results, and understand the main idea of performance management systems; - can analyze the changes within the business environment and their effects on the work of a controller and trends in accounting.
content: The concepts, evolution, and trends in management accounting. Management control and basics of performance measurement. Key challenges of strategic cost management and value chain analysis. Activity-based costing, its use in product-related decision-making, and its relations to customer profitability analysis. Competitor accounting. Financial planning. The work of a controller and skill requirements.
prerequisites: CS31A0102 Basic Course in Cost Management or equivalent knowledge. If the prerequisites are not fulfilled, the student must read the following book before the course begins: Neilimo, K. & Uusi-Rauva, E. Johdon laskentatoimi. Edita Oyj, Helsinki 2005, 6th Edition or newer.
learningMaterial: Course book: Järvenpää, M., Länsiluoto, A., Partanen, V. & Pellinen, J. Talousohjaus ja kustannuslaskenta. Sanoma Pro Oy, Helsinki 2015/2017. In addition, lecture notes and other assigned reading. Complementary literature: Suomala, P., Manninen, O. & Lyly-Yrjänäinen, J. Laskentatoimi johtamisen tukena. Edita, Helsinki 2011/2018. Horngren, C.T., Datar, S.M. & Foster, G. Cost Accounting, A Managerial Emphasis. Prentice Hall, 2006, 12th Edition or newer.
evaluationCriteria: Grade 0-5, evaluation 0-100 points. Individual and case assignments 50%, exam 50%. All assignments must be passed to obtain final grade.
workload: Lectures 24h, seminar 2h, exercises 4h, preparation for lectures and exercises 30h, individual assignments and case assignment in groups 45h, preparation for exam and taking the exam 55h. Total workload 160 h.

name: Structures, Materials and Production Processes
learningOutcomes: The student is able to - identify the differences between production techniques and technologies in product design - select appropriate structures, productions methods and materials in a design project - define the effects of the chosen production method on the end product's price and qualities
prerequisites: Details available in Completion methods under the header Teaching
learningMaterial: Details available in Completion methods under the header Teaching
workload: Details under the header Teaching

name: Supplier Development and Relationship Management
learningOutcomes: The aim of the course is to examine the concepts of supplier development (SD) and supplier relationship management (SRM) from different perspectives. Depending of their previous studies, students can gain new knowledge and/or deepen their understanding of these topics through assigned readings and academic literature in the field. In addition to the academic perspectives, the students can gain knowledge about practical issues, such as practices of supplier relationship management and future trends of supplier relationship management. After completing the course, the students are able to critically assess and analyze the literature and practical issues and trends related to supplier development and relationship management. Students should know the recent trends, tools and sustainability-related practices of supplier development and relationship management.
content: - The concepts and theories of supplier development and supplier relationship management including related sustainability perspectives - Evolving trends, practices and tools of supplier development and relationship management
prerequisites: B.Sc. (Econ. & Bus.Adm.) studies. For exchange students, B.Sc. studies related to operations management, supply chain management, supply management or similar.
learningMaterial: Educational videos. Assigned readings will be announced at the beginning of the course. In addition, independent searching of relevant and topical scientific journal articles in databases, and practical material /writings in internet.
evaluationCriteria: Grading 0-5, evaluation 0-100 points. The final grade consists of eight small exams in Moodle (40%) and a written report (60%). To pass the course, students must achieve at least 50% of the maximum points in each individual assignment. This means that at least 50% must be obtained separately in each of the eight small exams (not as a combined total) and at least 50% in the written report.
workload: A self-learning course conducted via Moodle (no contact teaching, but the teacher instructs students via Moodle messages every week). Eight small exams (quizzes) in Moodle and preparation for the small exams, 60 hours. Independent reading assignments and a written report, student-driven content creation, and discussion, 100 hours. Total workload: 160 hours. Offered twice in an academic year: 3rd period and summer course.

name: Supply Chain Design and Management
learningOutcomes: Upon completion of this course, students should be able to evaluate logistics operations and their integration into supply chains, assess the environmental impacts of supply chain operations, and understand the role of digitalization in enhancing efficiency and sustainability. Students will be able to map the supply chain design and assess suppliers. They will gain the ability to design plans for sustainable supply chains and effectively communicate their objectives. Students will also learn to apply established frameworks for supply chain development and efficiently search for, evaluate, and utilize relevant information and resources. After completing the course, students will be able to: 1. Evaluate logistics operations to develop the supply chains 2. Assess environmental impacts of supply chain operations 3. Understand role of digitalization in supply chain development 4. Design plan and communicate goals of sustainable supply chains 5. Define a supply chain decarbonization strategy 6. Use supply chain development frameworks 7. Search and assess available information for supply chain development
content: Characteristics of supply networks, business models in supply chains, role of logistic service providers, resources embedded to the supply chains, design and integration of operations, development of supply chain processes. Decarbonization footprint audit for supply chain. Environmental impact of logistics operations. Digital platforms and architectures of supply chains management.
prerequisites: Bachelor's studies. For exchange students: B.Sc. studies related to operations management, supply chain management, supply management or similar are required.
learningMaterial: 1. Lecture material. 2. Other course material will be announced.
evaluationCriteria: Grading scale General scale, 0-5. Essay 60 %, Group Assignment: 25%, Individual assignments: 15%. Each course component needs to be passed to pass the course overall.
workload: Lectures and workshops 18 h, essay 30 h, independent study 52 h, practical assignment and readings 60 h. Total workload 160 h.

name: Sustainability and Impact in Business Research
learningOutcomes: The student becomes aware of the role and impact of their research in the context of business sustainability and responsibility. The student can position, assess, and discuss their research regarding its direct and indirect impact to multiple stakeholders in business and society.
content: Course in organized in blended mode. Seminar presentation and participation to a seminar.
prerequisites: The course is available only for students accepted to the Doctoral Programme in Business and Management at LUT Business School.
learningMaterial: Handed out during the course.
evaluationCriteria: Final grade: Pass / fail, based on the returned written essay.
workload: Students return a written essay and participate to and present in the course seminar.

name: Sustainability Reporting and Communication
learningOutcomes: By the end of the course, students will be able 1. to understand sustainability reporting landscape 2. to identify and analyze alternative ways to communicate sustainability as part of the business strategy
content: Main content is connected to course aims: 1. Understand sustainability reporting and the shift from voluntary to mandatory 2. Learn how to prepare and write a sustainability report 3. Learn and analyze alternatives ways to communicate sustainability and understand the strategic value of sustainability communication
prerequisites: B.Sc level studies.
learningMaterial: Research articles and other materials will be published in Moodle.
evaluationCriteria: Assessment on the scale 0-5. 1. Essays, analyses and multiple choice test 30% 2. Preparing a sustainability report 40% 3. Case analysis related to sustainability communication 30%
workload: Independent learning based on the course materials, F2F and on-line lectures, videos with short lectures, case studies, stimulating discussion, (50 h). Online tests and assignments (40h). Preparing a sustainability report and a case analysis (70 h). Total workload 160 hours.

name: Financial Statement Analysis
learningOutcomes: By the end of the course, students will be able to: - pay attention to essential factors of financial statement which can affect interpretation - analyze, interpret and explain financial situation of a company using common key ratios of financial statement analysis - evaluate the level of key ratios using mark scales and industry statistics - choose suitable key ratios for a case with motivation by literature - match effects of company's operational environment and industry to financial situation - search for company's financial statement data and key ratios from different sources, among others financial statement databases. General aim of the course is to improve personal skills of the student: - write a case report using common instructions of scientific writing
content: Content and adjustment of financial statement. Analysis of financial statement. Ratios of financial statement analysis, interpretation and utilization. Cash flow statement. Databases of financial statements.
prerequisites: A250A0250 Basic Course in Financial Accounting
learningMaterial: 1. Yritystutkimus ry: Yritystutkimuksen tilinpäätösanalyysi, 2017 or newer 2. Kallunki, J-P.: Tilinpäätösanalyysi, 2022 or newer 3. Kaisanlahti, T., Leppiniemi, J., Leppiniemi, R.: Tilinpäätöksen tulkinta, 2021 or newer 4. Salmi, I.: Mitä tilinpäätös kertoo?, 2020 or newer 5. Kallunki, J-P., Lantto, A-M., Sahlström, P.: Tilinpäätösanalyysi IFRS-maailmassa, 2008 or newer 6. Lecture materials
evaluationCriteria: Grade 0-5, evaluation 0-100 points, written case report 100%
workload: Lectures 28 h, exercises 28 h, independent exercises and preparation for lectures 5 h, written case report 42 h, 1st period. Written case report 55 h, feedback lecture 2 h, 2nd period. Total workload 160 h.

name: Basic Course in Auditing
learningOutcomes: Students learn to understand the basics of auditing, internal auditing, to define regulation that is related to auditing and to understand and to recognize reports of auditor. Moreover, students learn to understand the current changes in the field of auditing and the essential features of the auditing profession.
content: Regulation of auditing. Tasks and actitivites of auditing. Auditing obligation and competence of auditor. Audit reports. Auditing as a profession. Internal control. ESG reporting and it's assurance.
prerequisites: A250A0750 Financial Statement Analysis
learningMaterial: 1. Tomperi, S.: Tilintarkastus - Normeista käytäntöön, 2018 or newer 2. Ratsula, N.: Yrityksen sisäinen valvonta, 2021 or newer 3. Lecture materials 4. Other literature announced by the lecturers
evaluationCriteria: Assessment scale and assessment methods: Grade 0-5, evaluation 0-100 points, learning tasks of group 50%, individual learning task 30% and examination in Exam 20%.
workload: Teaching methods: Lectures and exercises 28 h, preparing for the lectures and exercises, learning tasks of group work 67 h, personal learning task including a reflection on guest lectures and an examination in Exam 65 h, 4th period. Total workload 160 h.

name: Auditing - Theory and Practise
learningOutcomes: During the course students get more through understand of auditing and familiarize themselves with audit research. At the end of the course a student is expected to be able to: - know different phases of audit process - know the audit quality system and responsibility of an auditor - analyze audit research
content: Audit planning and audit process, international standards of auditing, quality control and auditors' liability, auditors' role during problem situations. Theory of auditing, audit research.
prerequisites: A250A0850 Tilintarkastuksen perusteet
learningMaterial: 1. Halonen K., Steiner M-L.: Tilintarkastusprosessi käytännössä, 2010 2. International standards of auditing 3. Lecture material 4. Other literature announced by the lecturer
evaluationCriteria: Grade 0-5, evaluation 0-100 points, learning tasks of group 40 %, personal learning tasks 60 %.
workload: Lectures and exercises 28 h, preparing for the lectures and exercises, learning tasks of group work 72 h, personal learning tasks 60 h, 4th period. Total workload 160 h.

name: Valuation of Financial Securities: Theory and Practice
learningOutcomes: At the end of this course a student is expected to have a concise overall understanding of valuation of financial securities and the sources of value creation. After successful completion of this course, the student will be able to: demonstrate advanced level skills in describing corporate finance theories outline the determinants of financing needs and optimal capital structure evaluate the empirical aspects of corporate finance and asset valuation estimate valuation of corporate debt and equity under uncertainty design and carry out an investment analysis project from start to the end, justify the choice of methods, and discuss the consequences of these choices. present and defend the obtained results of the project in a systematic professional way in a written report and in a seminar.
content: Student in this course learn the step-by-step methods of valuation and create an investment analysis report based on their results. The presentations of the produced reports and subsequent findings is an integral part of the course. The topics include: Basics of Valuation Corporate strategy and sources of value Interpreting and using financial statements Forecasting of financial statements Discounted cash flow models Estimating cost of capital/discount rate Comparable or relative valuation models Business analytics models for finance
prerequisites: This course is primarily intended for 2 nd year M.Sc. students in Strategic Finance and Analytics who have either completed or enrolled into following compulsory courses of MSF programme.
learningMaterial: Lecture notes provided by the teacher Academic articles and documents provided at moodle Any textbook on ‘Valuation’ or 'Corporate Finance' Selected chapters of following textbooks
evaluationCriteria: Grade 1-5 on the basis of 100 points. Investment valuation report (60 points), online quizzes (20 points), class contribution, discussion and presentation (20 points). To pass the course, a student needs to obtain a minimum of 50% of the points in each task and attend the presentation seminars physically in Lappeenranta.
workload: Lectures and online workshops 30 h, preparation for lectures 20 h, preparation for quizzes and participation 24 h, preparation of report and presentation 78 h, presentation seminar 8 h, Total workload 160 h

name: Additive Manufacturing and 3D Printing (Advanced)
learningOutcomes: Student will know following fields of additive manufacturing (aka 3D printing) after passing course: - characteristics of materials used in AM, - different properties of AM parts, - comprehensive understanding of product design for AM (DfAM), - details of simulation driven DfAM. - latest knowledge of AM technologies and materials, - have skills that are needed to help reform technological readiness in different industries - have understanding Additive manufacturing solutions for advanced energy sector industry in the future
content: In this course a practical approach is taken to understand multiple steps in design and preparation work. The focus is on the metal additive manufacturing and its special characteristics. Different DfAM steps are presented more detailed. Guidelines for support structures and light weight design are given. Material selection and effect of material properties in the strength (or function) of the structure is discussed.
prerequisites: Advanced knowledge level of engineering sciences.
learningMaterial: Course material provided in Moodle during course. Further reading e.g. Gibson, I., Rosen, D. W., Stucker, B.: Additive Manufacturing Technologies.
evaluationCriteria: Grade 0-5, seminar works 50%, exam 50%
workload: Lectures 20 h, periods 1-2. Tutorials and guiding 10 h, periods 1-2. Individual work 105 h. Total workload 135 h. The course is suitable for on-line learning.

name: Advanced Additive Manufacturing and 3D Printing
learningOutcomes: Student will know following fields of additive manufacturing (aka 3D printing) after passing course: - characteristics of materials used in AM, - different properties of AM parts, - comprehensive understanding of product design for AM (DfAM), - details of simulation driven DfAM. - latest knowledge of AM technologies and materials, - have skills that are needed to help reform technological readiness in different industries - have understanding Additive manufacturing solutions for advanced energy sector industry in the future
content: In this course a practical approach is taken to understand multiple steps in design and preparation work. The focus is on the metal additive manufacturing and its special characteristics. Different DfAM steps are presented. Guidelines for support structures and light weight design are given. Material selection and effect of material properties in the strength (or function) of the structure is discussed.
prerequisites: Advanced knowledge level of engineering sciences.
learningMaterial: Course material provided in Moodle during course. Further reading e.g. Gibson, I., Rosen, D. W., Stucker, B.: Additive Manufacturing Technologies.
evaluationCriteria: Grade 0-5, Exercises 60%, exam 40%
workload: Lectures 20 h, periods 1-2. Tutorials and guiding 10 h, periods 1-2. Individual and group work 105 h. Total workload 135 h. The course is suitable for on-line learning.

name: Advanced Data Analysis and Machine Learning
learningOutcomes: The student is able to 1) pre-process, visualise and analyse multivariate synthetic and real-world data, 2) understand and use state-of-the-art regression methods and machine learning and 3) apply the studied methods to implement artificial intelligence in the form of machine learning and perform data analysis, analyse the results and report the findings.
content: Characteristics and pre-processing of data, linear and nonlinear dimensionality reduction. Logistic, multivariate statistical methods and advanced extensions of the methods. Deep neural networks, semi-supervised learning and generative models. Case-based topics on data analysis and machine learning. Company cooperation: no direct cooperation. Use of AI applications: readily available AI tools can be used for checking the language of written reports.
prerequisites: Ability to program in Matlab or Python.
learningMaterial: Lecture material, recorded videos and demonstrations in Moodle and additional literature.
evaluationCriteria: 0 - 5. Written exams 40%, exercises and workshops 30%, projects 30%.

name: Advanced Materials in Adsorption and Ion Exchange
learningOutcomes: Towards the completion of this course, the student is expected to fulfill the following criteria: -To describe the conventional and novel adsorption/ion-exchange materials. -To describe the conventional and novel applications of adsorption and ion-exchange. -To select an appropriate adsorption/ion-exchange material for a particular purpose according to the composition of the water to be purified. -To understand the theory and the mechanism in adsorption processes. -Use of theoretical models to describe the adsorption kinetics, isotherms, and thermodynamics. -To solve the adsorption/ion exchange based water purification case studies.
content: - Introduction to adsorption and ion exchange theories. - Learning the types and properties of conventional and novel adsorption and ion exchange materials and their applications in water research. - Learning to evaluate the economic and environmental aspects of the production and use of different adsorption and ion exchange materials. - Learning the surface reactions and theories behind the adsorption and ion exchange phenomena. - Ultimately, identifying the necessary tools to effectively deal with various environmental issues and industrial challenges using advanced materials in adsorption and ion exchange processes. -Case studies relevant to the process, implementation to water treatment and seminar works to provide in-depth knowledge of adsorption/ion-exchange-based water purification. -Carrying out individual and group works, including problem-based learning (PBL), quizzes and assignments.
prerequisites: BJ03A1040-Advanced Materials in Adsorption and Ion Exchange

name: Advanced Studies in in Global Communications and Asia
learningOutcomes: The learning outcomes for the course are: (1) ability to describe and understand key concepts and approaches related to global communications and Asia, focusing on cultural and social phenomena such as Hallyu, Bollywood or Cool Japan. (2) ability to compare and contrast different models and theories on media, communications and soft power in context of Asia and related cultural and social phenomena. (3) ability to analyse Asian cultural and social phenomena from perspective of global media and communications. (4) During the course the participants also get practice in writing academic texts and arguing for their views through their texts.
content: This literature course focuses on studying key concepts and approaches related to global communications and Asia in the context of media, communications and soft power. During the course the students read a wide variety of literature on different Asian countries and explore how questions soft power and media are played out in different contexts. All use of AI tools for the course work must be carefully documented according to separate instructions provided in the course Moodle site.

name: Climate Action – Sustainable design and production Module 4: Climate Actions
learningOutcomes: After having passed this course module the student is able to: - list the main barriers to sustainable decision making and methods to overcome them - examine specific climate actions related to consumer and industrial products - review end of life processes which promote sustainability and enable a circular economy
content: Module 4 brings together all the elements for previous modules to enable better decision making and promote everyday climate action. It begins by introducing the roles of individuals, industries and engineering specialists in promoting sustainability through the products we purchase and use. And it ends by exploring various options to secure a sustainable end of life of common consumer and industrial products.

name: Introduction to Generative AI and its Applications
learningOutcomes: On completion of this module students should be able to: - Reflect on the current methods and tools of Generative AI - Implement the principles of prompts engineering - Identify the opportunities for adoption of Generative AI within organisations - Evaluate the potential benefits and challenges of Generative AI use
content: The course is designed to provide basic knowledge on principles and use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in various industries. It offers a perspective on the identification of opportunities for its application and the related challenges. Several examples of applications are given as well as the requirements presented for the successful implementation of AI systems. Course contents: 1. Basic concepts and definitions of Generative AI 2. Principles of prompts engineering 3. Review of Generative AI tools and technologies 4. Business applications of Generative AI in the selected sectors (marketing, manufacturing, healthcare, transport) 5. Strengths, risks and limitations of Generative AI 6. Requirements for implementation of Generative AI systems in organisation 7. Organisational and technical implications of Generative AI adoption 8. Ethical considerations of AI use
