evaluationCriteria: Grade 0-5. Participation to lectures and activity during them 10 %, groupwork and activity in groupwork sessions 20 % submitted groupwork exercises 20 %, submitted individual exercises 50%
workload: Attending to lectures 6h, attending to group work sessions 6h, groupwork and related exercises 30h, reading of the course material 30h, individual exercises 20h, individual work 40h

name: Laboratory Course in Electrical Engineering 1
learningOutcomes: Upon completion of the course the student will be able to: * work safely in practical tasks in electrical engineering and manage electrical risk in the workplace * identify typical electric, electronic and installation components * use multimeters and oscilloscopes * design and implement test setup and analyze the operation of electric devices based on measurements * read and produce technical documentation of electric circuits and installations.
content: Electrical safety, first aid and electrical shock, professional working attitude and practices in different laboratory environments at LUT, multimeter and oscilloscope in typical measurement tasks, measurement of electrical power, measurement automation and data acquisition, measurement uncertainty and typical error sources, typical components in electrical engineering and electronics, various practical design and measurement tasks.
learningMaterial: Materials are based on accepted industrial and scientific documents and will be delivered for students in Moodle. Literature: Silvonen, Kimmo. Sähkötekniikka ja elektroniikka. Helsinki, Otatieto, 511 s. 2003. Ahoranta, J., Sähkötekniikka, 2015, Sanoma Pro Aura, Lauri 1996. Teoreettinen sähkötekniikka ja sähkökoneiden perusteet. 2 uud. p. Porvoo: WSOY. 448 s. ISBN 951-0-21385-3 Aumala, Olli 1985. Mittaustekniikka, osa 1 Mittaustekniikan perusteet. 3. uus. p. Porvoo: Otakustantamo. 112 s. ISBN 951-671-143-X
evaluationCriteria: 0–5. Moodle assignments, laboratory work and reports 100 %.
workload: Moodle, laboratory work and reports, 1st – 4th period. Independent study 60 h.Total workload 108 h. The course cannot be completed remotely. Teaching at the Lappeenranta campus.

name: Laboratory Course in Electrical Engineering 2
learningOutcomes: The course strengthens the student’s theoretical knowledge and practical skills on basics of electrical engineering by working in the laboratory. Upon completion of the course the student will be able to: 1. work in a laboratory in safe and professional manner, including risk assessment 2. make basic electrical measurements (current, voltage, power, resistance etc.) on different measurement setups and devices 3. design measurement setup including selection of measurement devices 4. design and read electric circuit diagrams 5. analyse measurement data and estimate the reliability of the results 6. write measurement documentation/report. In addition to the general aims described above, the student will be able to learn the work-specific aims described in the work instructions.
content: Basics of electrical engineering by practical measurements in the laboratory in small groups. Design of measurement plan, selection and use of measurement devices, safe working methods in the laboratory, estimation of the reliability of the results, analysis on measurements and documentation. Laboratory works are related e.g. to following subjects: safe working in the laboratory and use of laboratory equipment, dimensioning of the components, RLC-circuit, three-phase system, transformer, control- and automation, electrical drives, electrical installations in buildings and related commissioning inspections.
prerequisites: Recommended: BL10A9000 Laboratory Course in Electrical Engineering 1, BL10A0101 Basics of Electrical Engineering, BL30A0001 Electric Circuits
learningMaterial: Materials are based on accepted industrial and scientific documents and will be delivered for students in Moodle. Literature: Silvonen, Kimmo. Sähkötekniikka ja elektroniikka. Helsinki, Otatieto, 511 s. 2003. Ahoranta, J., Sähkötekniikka, 2015, Sanoma Pro Aura, Lauri 1996. Teoreettinen sähkötekniikka ja sähkökoneiden perusteet. 2 uud. p. Porvoo: WSOY. 448 s. ISBN 951-0-21385-3 Aumala, Olli 1985. Mittaustekniikka, osa 1 Mittaustekniikan perusteet. 3. uus. p. Porvoo: Otakustantamo. 112 s. ISBN 951-671-143-X
evaluationCriteria: 0-5. Preliminary assignments, laboratory work, analysis on measurements and documentation 100%. Work-specific weights on assessment are given in work instructions. To pass the course, every work has to be passed with a grade 1 at minimum.
workload: Laboratory work, preliminary assignments and measurement reports individually and in small groups. Requires independent information retrieval. Introductory lecture 1 h, 1st period. Laboratory measurements approx. 30 h and independent work approx. 77 h (preliminary assignments, measurement analysis and written reports). 1st-4th period. Total workload 108 h. Course can not be completed remotely. Teaching takes place on Lappeenranta campus.

name: Laboratory Course in Electrical Engineering 3
learningOutcomes: Upon completion of the course the student will be able to: 1. Work in a laboratory in a safe and professional manner, 2. design a measurement or research setup, including the selection of measurement instruments and sensors, 3. design and read electric circuit diagrams 4. Evaluate measurement uncertainty 5. Interpret measurement results and draw conclusions from them. 6. Work as a member of a project group and complete a small project
content: Practical measurements and laboratory work related to the following areas of expertise: sensors and measurement technology, the operational principle of an inverter, automation, electrical motor, commissioning of an electrical drive, electrical installations and commissioning tests in buildings. Writing a measurement plan, choosing measurement instruments and carrying out measurements safely. Documenting measurements and estimating measurement uncertainty.
prerequisites: It is recommended that the student is already able to: 1. Work in an electrical engineering laboratory in a safe manner and with a professional, safe working attitude 2. Measure voltage, current, power and resistance using a multimeter, and carry out basic measurements using an oscilloscope, and use laboratory power supplies 3. Identify and use common electrical and electronic components 4. Interpret simple electrical schematics 5. Write simple code in a programming language and run the code in a microcontroller.
learningMaterial: Materials are based on accepted industrial and scientific documents and will be delivered for students in Moodle. Literature: Silvonen, Kimmo. Sähkötekniikka ja elektroniikka. Helsinki, Otatieto, 511 s. 2003. Ahoranta, J., Sähkötekniikka, 2015, Sanoma Pro Aura, Lauri 1996. Teoreettinen sähkötekniikka ja sähkökoneiden perusteet. 2 uud. p. Porvoo: WSOY. 448 s. ISBN 951-0-21385-3 Aumala, Olli 1985. Mittaustekniikka, osa 1 Mittaustekniikan perusteet. 3. uus. p. Porvoo: Otakustantamo. 112 s. ISBN 951-671-143-X
evaluationCriteria: 0-5, continuous assessment. The laboratory assignments to be completed during autumn make up 50% of the final grade, and the project work during spring makes up the remaining 50%. Assessment of the laboratory assignments consists of the preliminary assignments, laboratory work and the results of the laboratory work. Project work will be assessed based on the progress of the project during the spring, as well as the final presentation of the project.
workload: During autumn: laboratory assignments on specific subjects in small groups. The assignments consist of preliminary assignments, laboratory work and analyzing results. Laboratory assignments consist of six areas of expertise, with six hours of laboratory work on each. Total workload during autumn is 54 hours. During spring: a project to be carried out in small groups. Total workload in the project is 54 hours. Total workload 108 h.

name: Laboratory Course in Electrical Engineering for DIODI Students
learningOutcomes: Upon completion of the course the student will be able to: 1. execute safe electrical measurements 2. plan and execute measurements using the instruments in the laboratory on electric drives, motors, power electronics and/or electric networks, 3. analyse measurement results and draw conclusions from them, 4. describe the laboratory work task, measurement setup, results and analysis.
content: Electrical measurements, electrical machines, power factor, reactive power compensation, quality of supply, basic principles of frequency converter, switch mode power supplies. Use of AI applications AI applications can be used according to the general guidelines of LUT.
prerequisites: Basics of electrical engineering. Ability to perform basic electrical measurements using multimeter and oscilloscope. Teamwork skills.
learningMaterial: The learning material is based on the latest research and is distributed to students in Moodle.
evaluationCriteria: 0-5. Based on laboratory measurements and reports.
workload: Introductory lecture at Lappeenranta campus, 1 h, during the orientation day. Preliminary report, laboratory measurements at Lappeenranta campus and final report during 1.-4. periods. There are four laboratory assignments, 1 ECTS each. Total workload 108 h. Laboratory assignments are made in groups of three students. Attendance in the laboratory measurements is compulsory.

name: Control Systems, Introduction
learningOutcomes: Upon completion of the course the student will be able to: 1. form differential equations from dynamic systems and form transfer functions/state space models from differential equations, 2. study the stability of dynamic systems and time domain performance, 3. evaluate dynamic properties of (1st and 2nd order) systems and tune these using simple controllers,
content: Dynamic models of linear systems. Transfer functions. Laplace domain. Basic concepts and analyses of control engineering. Compensators and controllers. Usual process models. Duality of time and frequency domains. Analytic tuning of a controller. State space models. Use of Matlab/Simulink programs in control problems.
prerequisites: Basics on differential equations, basics on complex numbers.
learningMaterial: Lecture notes. Additionally, one of the following books (where applicable) is recommended: Franklin, Powell, Emami-Naeini: Feedback Control of Dynamic Systems. Dorf: Modern Control Systems. Shinners: Modern Control System Theory and Design. Virkkunen, Jouko: Säätötekniikan matematiikkaa. Moodle.
evaluationCriteria: 0–5, examination 100 % (EXAM electronic examination + Moodle). Possibility to get max. 10 additional points from homework.
workload: 12 h of lectures, 12 h of tutorials, 3rd period. 14 h of lectures, 14 h of tutorials, 4th period. Voluntary homework. Written midterms or examination. Total workload 81 h.

name: Work Experience in Bachelor's Degree in Finland
learningOutcomes: After completing the course, the student is familiar with the job application processes of companies and organizations and can prepare the necessary job application documents. The student has been introduced to a work environment representing their field of study and knows, through practical personal experience, what paid work is, what it is like to work for an employer, what the basic rules of working life are from the employee's perspective, and how to operate within a work community.
content: The student applies to a company in Finland for (summer) work, works there as an employee under an employment contract, requests a work certificate, and gets the work approved as work experience for a Bachelor of Science in Technology degree. The work to be approved as work experience must be related to the student's field of study, and the duration of the employment must be at least 4 weeks in a full-time position or an equivalent total number of hours (at least 150 hours). Completing a bachelor's thesis is not accepted as work experience. At the discretion of the work experience coordinator, work done before the start of studies, which has not been included in the student's previous degrees, can also be accepted as work experience.
evaluationCriteria: Pass/Fail, work experience report 100 %.
workload: The approval of work experience is applied for using the application form available on eLUT, which is submitted to the Moodle platform "Work experience in chemical engineering." The application must include a work experience report (form available on eLUT) and a copy of the work certificate. The total workload is 54 hours, including 10 hours for job search and recruitment, 15 hours for tasks related to starting the employment (e.g., orientation, rules of employment and the workplace), 24 hours for observing the functions of the work community alongside working (e.g., methods of organizing work/production, management, working methods of the work community/teams, social activities at the workplace), and 5 hours for the written work experience report (length 2-3 pages).

name: Project Work in Engineering Mathematics 1
learningOutcomes: The student advances their knowledge of mathematical theory or gains practical knowledge from applying mathematical skills in analyzing, modelling or optimizing a problem related to their field of studies. The course prepares the student for advanced studies leading up to the writing of a B.Sc. thesis. The student gains insight into the role of digitalization and mathematical models in the future life, society and business. The student may introduce themselves to the use of AI tools to assist problem-solving and writing.
content: A specific project is done as either a theoretical study, laboratory experiments or in a suitable commercial co-operator. The project is planned with the supervisor and may consist of laboratory work, literature research and/or theoretical studies, reporting, article writing or problem-solving in industry. The course underlines the importance of understanding the computer models of the student’s field that are driving much of industry and business and the role of digitalization in changing business models. Company cooperation The project can be done for a company. Use of AI tools AI tools are part of the "computer models" and can be studied in the course.
learningMaterial: Basic guidelines are available on Moodle.
evaluationCriteria: Basic guidelines are available on Moodle.
workload: Non-stop, 1-4 ja kesä Contact teaching. Individual or group study, brief written report and project presentation.

name: Basics of technical calculation and engineering mechanics Module 1: Basics of Technical Mathematics
learningOutcomes: The student can rehearse fundamental skills required for university mathematics in this course. After completing the course, the student can plot and interpret the graphs of functions, solve simple equations and systems of equations, calculate derivatives and integrals of simple functions, and perform the basic operations in vector and matrix computing. In addition, the student can apply the mathematical skills used in this course to solve simple engineering problems.
content: Mathematical functions, equations and systems of equations, derivative, integral, vectors and matrices, engineering applications of the previous.
evaluationCriteria: Grading scale: Pass-Fail, 100 % assignments.
workload: Independent learning and assignments. Total workload 54 h.

name: Basics of technical calculation and engineering mechanics Module 4: Basics of FEM
learningOutcomes: Student understands the concept of finite element method and applications of finite element method. Student can form systems of equations related to computational elements and represent the systems of equations in matrix form. Student can perform a simple mechanical analysis with MATLAB-software. Student also understands how finite element method is related to partial differential equations. Student also acquires basic understanding of visualization of a vector quantity.
content: Finite element method, matrices, systems of equations, using MATLAB-plugin to perform finite element analysis, vector quantity visualization.
evaluationCriteria: Grading scale: Pass-Fail, 100 % assignments.
workload: Independent learning and assignments. Total workload 54 h.

name: Basics of technical calculation and engineering mechanics Module 5: Basics of Mechanics
learningOutcomes: After completing the module, the student is able to analyze the forces and moments that act on a body and define the support reactions required for equilibrium. The student understands the concepts of distributed loading and friction forces and is able to calculate their magnitude. The student understands when the nature of the problem in question changes from static to dynamic.
content: Division of forces to components, combining the effects of forces, calculation and combination of moments. Equilibrium of a particle and rigid body. Distributed loadings and friction. Kinematics of a particle.
evaluationCriteria: Grading scale: Pass-Fail, 100 % assignments.
workload: Independent learning and assignments. Total workload 54 h.

name: Technical Computing Software
learningOutcomes: After the course, the student is an elementary-level user of some computational development environment and is familiar with finding its documentation and implementing numerical methods using the development environment. The student has been introduced to software engineering and can define and solve simple computational problems using the development environment or a spreadsheet program. The students can use and produce technical information and assess information produced by themselves and others.
content: The course introduces the student to basics of Matlab: Interface of the integrated development environment (IDE), conditional structures, array structures, plotting curves and surfaces, loop structures. In addition, Simulink and a spreadsheet program is used for problem-solving. Basic applications in numerical analysis, such as root finding, optimization and solving simple differential equations, with examples for engineering. Documenting the development process and writing formulas using LaTeX. Company cooperation The course project may be done for a company. Use of AI tools AI tools can be used to assist in problem-solving and writing. As an optional topic, you may train your own AI to solve a simple problem.
prerequisites: It is recommended that the student has some sort of introduction to programming before taking this course.
learningMaterial: Lecture material and other material announced during the course. Optionally applicable parts of Matlab Academy online service.
evaluationCriteria: 0-5. Exercises 50 %, project work and seminar 50 %.
workload: Demos 20 h, exercises 16 h, homework and self-study 36 h. Project and seminar 36 hours. Total workload 108 hours.

name: Technology, communities and society
learningOutcomes: After completing the course, students: Will understand social scientific thinking and perspectives on digital communication technologies. Are familiar with current social scientific research literature on group dynamics and social issues in digital environments. Will know how to review digital environments from social scientifically essential perspectives, such as a sense of community, loneliness, and well-being. Will understand the significance of social scientific theories in research on digitalisation and communication technologies.
content: Content: Current social scientific research on the impacts of communication technologies on individuals and communities at different life domains. The role of digitalisation in behaviour, thinking and emotions from the perspectives of psychological and social factors. Group dynamics and social structures in digitalized society: e.g., social relationships and online communities, social identity and social bubbles, the role of technologies in social interaction. Reviewing digitalization from the perspectives of social sustainability and wellbeing: e.g., work well-being, loneliness, online hate and harassment. Use of AI applications. During the course we will practice the use of artificial intelligence and communication technology as a part of group work.
learningMaterial: Attrill-Smith, A., Fullwood, C., Keep, M., & Kuss, D. J. (Eds.). (2019). The Oxford handbook of cyberpsychology. Oxford University Press. ( Parts IV–V ; pp 239-432; 194 pages) * Keipi, T., Näsi, M., Oksanen, A., & Räsänen, P. (2016). Online hate and harmful content: Cross-national perspectives. Taylor & Francis. (154 pages) * Nabi, R. L., & Myrick, J. G. (Eds.). (2023). Emotions in the digital world: Exploring affective experience and expression in online interactions. Oxford University Press. ( Parts III–V ; pp 153-462; 310 pages) * Gilson, L. L., O’Neill, T., & Maynard, M. T. (Eds.). (2023). Handbook of virtual work. Edward Elgar Publishing. Sundar, S. S. (2015). The handbook of the psychology of communication technology. John Wiley & Sons. Other scientific research literature. * Book exam -completion method cancelled academic year 2005-2006
evaluationCriteria: Numerical assessment on a scale of 0–5. Written group assignments based on lectures, group meetings, and research literature (100%).
workload: Attending lectures onsite (6 h), weekly group meetings (14h), independent study (55 h), and written group assignments (60 h). The course involves working in independently formed groups of 4–5 students. Please also reserve a time slot corresponding to the lectures for weekly group meetings (reading circle).

name: Laboratory Course of Thermodynamics
learningOutcomes: Upon completion of the course, the students will be able to write a consistent and well-defined research report following the principles of academic writing. Students will be able to measure the state values of a thermodynamic system, and apply these values to the principles of thermodynamics to study that system. Students will be able to apply the theory of thermodynamics into problem solving. Completion of the course supports the development of the following generic competences for working life: Team working skills, oral and written communication, project management.
content: Literature survey, laboratory work, and personal home work. In the literature survey, students familiarize themselves with the basic phenomena in thermodynamics: the history, persons behind the phenomena, how the phenomena is affecting at present, and how thermodynamic principles can be applied to real world applications. Students will write a literature report from a selected topic, present the report, and act as opponents for other students' reports. Laboratory works introduce students to measuring thermodynamic values and calculating process operating values, as well as applying mathematical calculations skill. Personal home work includes working on a thermodynamic system and applying its principles to problem solving. Course includes Power-to-X themes.
prerequisites: Recommended: BH20A0720 Engineering Thermodynamics
learningMaterial: Online material on Moodle, the handout “Thermodynamic tables”, enthalpy and entropy chart for steam. The relevant parts of Moran, M.J. & Shapiro, H.N.: Fundamentals of Engineering Thermodynamics, 5th ed. 2004 or later.
evaluationCriteria: 0 - 5. Three laboratory or project works that are evaluated, weight of each work in the evaluation: 33 %.
workload: 1st period: Introductory lecture 2 h, literature survey as group work and acting as an opponent for other reports 24 h. 2nd-3rd period: Preparation for laboratory measurements 2 h, laboratory measurements 2 h, preparation of a report from laboratory measurements 24 h. 3rd-4th period: Preparation of personal home work 27 h. Total workload 81 h.

name: Safety in Chemistry Laboratory
learningOutcomes: After the course the student - Recognizes the risk in laboratory work and can take into account them when working in laboratory - Understands the meaning of safety in laboratory work and how to put it into practice - Understands the whole chemical chain and is able to handle chemicals safely - Can choose the proper protection to work in the laboratory - Knows what to do in emergency or exceptional situation - Understands the roles, tasks and responsibilities of different persons, learns to work in group.
content: In the course it is told how to work safely in laboratory and which risks you should notice. In addition the chemical handling chain is explained and material safety data sheets are read. name: Water Treatment
searchTags: Written examination in the examination schedule
learningOutcomes: Upon completion of the course the students will be able to; 1. describe the production methods of the water used in power plants, 2. define the fundamental chemistry of water treatment, 3. describe the water quality measurement methods, 4. recognize the damages and danger situations caused by the water impurities, and 5. apply the information on water treatment processes essential for energy production. Completion of the course supports the development of the following generic competences for working life: mathematics and natural sciences, practical use of theory, independent work, problem solving.
content: The fundamentals of water treatment in brief. Water analytics. The production of process water and especially of makeup water for power plants. The influence of impurities on the water-steam cycle. Preservation of power plants.

name: Basic Professional Training Course on Nuclear Safety
learningOutcomes: Give a general view of nuclear safety field. After the course, the student can independently search and locate information on nuclear reactor and nuclear waste safety from all relevant disciplines. Expertise and skills: Know-how on own field, Knowledge of the research of own field, Knowledge of the history and development of own field, Team working skills, Working independently, Information retrieval, Ethicality
content: Based on IAEA course ”Basic Professional Training Course on Nuclear Safety”. General safety principles of nuclear power plants and nuclear waste management, authorities supervision, international rules. Deterministic and probabilistic methods of safety analysis. Practical solutions for nuclear waste management. Operation and maintenance of nuclear power plants. Safety culture. Accidents, emergency response and informing.
learningMaterial: The latest expert knowledge in the field is shared on the course's online learning platform Moodle.
evaluationCriteria: Pass/fail.
workload: Total workload 108 h.

name: Laboratory Course of Unit Processes
learningOutcomes: After a module the student can - make an experimental design that meets research goals - perform an experimental test in laboratory scale - work with laboratory scale equipment - assess the reliability of the experimental results - analyze experimental data, generate quantitative results and assess the reliability of them - write a technical – scientific report complying with given reporting instructions.
content: Four laboratory works in small groups: two related to mechanical and two to thermal unit processes.
prerequisites: Course BJ01A0020 Työturvallisuus laboratoriossa passed and BJ01A4011 Mekaaniset yksikköoperaatiot and BJ01A4030 Yksikköoperaatioiden mitoitus attended.
learningMaterial: Laboratory work instructions.

name: General and Inorganic Chemistry
learningOutcomes: Upon completion of the module, the student has been provided with the basic general understanding of university chemistry and chemical technology. After this course student can solve exercises from the following topics: 4 ects course: Moles, concentrations, gases, thermodynamics, redox-reactions, electrochemistry, reaction kinetics, equilibrium, pH and solubility, vapor pressure and colligative properties. 3 ects course: Moles, concentrations, gases, thermodynamics, redox-reactions, electrochemistry, kinetics and chemical equilibrium.
content: 4 ects course: Basics from: moles, concentration and reactions, solution, gases, termodynamics, Redox-reactions, electrochemistry, reaction kinetics, equilibrium, pH , buffer solution, solubility and colligative properties Course content is a more than what is learned in high school if all chemistry courses are studied. 3 ects course: Basics from: moles, concentration, reactions, solution, gases, termodynamics, Redox-reactions, electrochemistry, kinetics and chemical euilibrium.

workload: This 4 ETCS course is for students in chemical engineering (NOTE: course is taught only in Finnish). Tkk 1, Period 1. Lectures 31 h, exercises 14 h, self-study 63 h, total 108 h

name: Postgraduate Course in Environmental Engineering
learningOutcomes: Aim of the course is to induct the student into dedicated questions of environmental technology.
content: Course content and implementation varies case-by-case.

name: Laboratory Course of Environmental Measurements
learningOutcomes: Upon completion of the course the student is expected to be able to: 1. identify different measurement needs related to the state of the environment, 2. name key measurement methods for air pollution, wastewater and solid waste, and explain how they work, 3. use standards regarding pollution control, 4. select and use applicable measurement and sampling methods in practice, 5. calculate emission contents according to standards, 6. analyse measurement results, 7. identify sources of errors and assess their importance, and 8. report on pollution measurements in writing. The completion of the study module supports the development of the following general working life skills: mathematics and natural sciences, written communication, problem-solving, analytical thinking skills.
content: Three laboratory assignments carried out in groups, analysis of results.
prerequisites: BH60A0901 Ympäristömittaukset or equivalent knowledge. BJ01A0020 Safety in laboratory work course passed.
learningMaterial: Seppänen Olli, Air conditioning technology and indoor climate, LUT -library Baker Roger C, Flow measurement, ISBN 1 86058 348 2, 2001 Standards SFS-ISO 18400-104:2018:en ja SFS ISO 10381-1.
evaluationCriteria: 0 - 5. Laboratory assignment 100%.
workload: Introductory lecture 3 h, laboratory work approx. 105 h. Total workload 108 h.

name: Basic Course in Environmental Technology B
learningOutcomes: Upon completion of the course the student is expected to be able to 1. list the most important sustainability challenges posed by production and communities, 2. name the most typical ways of controlling sustainability challenges, 3. use environmental engineering terminology, 4. apply system analytical and life cycle thinking, and 5. explain how other technology fields are connected to environmental engineering.
content: Sustainability challenges at different spatial scales, related e.g. to production, consumption, solid waste, water use, air quality, energy transition, food systems, household consumption and the built environment. Technical solutions and steering mechanisms for the management of the sustainability challenges. The course also introduces life cycle thinking.
learningMaterial: Moodle, lecture materials, additional reading related to lecture topics
evaluationCriteria: 0-5. Examination in Moodle 100 %.
workload: 1st –2nd/3rd-4th period 22 h of lectures. 1st –2nd/3rd-4th period approx. 60 h of lecture quizzes. Total workload 82 h.

name: Digitalization in Retailing
learningOutcomes: Opintojakson suoritettuaan opiskelija osaa: - Selittää mitä digitaalinen transformaatio tarkoittaa - Analysoida digitaalisuuden vaikutuksia asiakkaiden ostokäyttäytymiseen - Kehittää markkinoinnin ja myynnin käytänteitä vastaamaan paremmin asiakkaiden muuttuneita ostopäätösprosesseja
content: Kurssi käsittelee kaupan alan digitalisaatiota kolmesta näkökulmasta: 1) digitaalisaatio kaupan alan strategiassa, 2) digitalisaatio kaupan alan markkinoinnissa ja 3) digitalisaatio kaupan alan ostokäyttäytymisessä. Kurssilla käydään läpi sekä strategisen että taktisen tason asioita, joita kaupan alan toimijat kohtaavat implementoidessaan digitaalista markkinointia.
prerequisites: Suositellaan: Markkinoinnin perusteet. Mikäli opintojaksolle ilmoittautuneiden lukumäärä ylittää maksimin, voidaan etusijalle asettaa ne, joilla on markkinoinnin perusteet suoritettuna.
learningMaterial: Luentomoniste, luennoitsijoiden jakamat artikkelit ja caset Chaffey, D., & Smith, P.R. (2017). Digital Marketing Excellence: Planning, Optimizing and Integrating Online Marketing (5th Ed.), Routledge. Kotler, P., Kartajaya, H., Setiawan, I. (2017). Marketing 4.0: Moving from Traditional to Digital. Wiley.
evaluationCriteria: Läsnäolo luennoilla 25%, yksilötyö 75%
workload: Verkkokurssi. Osallistuminen luennoille ja yksilötyö.

name: Work placement
learningOutcomes: Upon completion of this trainee period student can apply the knowledge and skills gained in Digital Retailing studies to working life. In addition, student gets acquainted with the trainee organization and understands its operations and key principles guiding the organization.
content: The trainee period corresponds to one-month full-time working, but also, part-time working arrangements are possible. Trainee period is carried out in digital retailing related work tasks in a company, public sector or other organization. Before the trainee period the student ensures the suitability of the work and considers her/his own objectives for the trainee period. After the trainee period student writes out a report where she/he considers the trainee period as part of her/his university studies and evaluates the progression of her/his working-life skills.
workload: Harjoitteluraportti. Lisätietoja harjoittelusta antaa Kaupan liiton koulutussuunnittelija Moona Naakka, p. 0469210857, moona.naakka@kauppa.fi

name: Distribution and Retail Management
learningOutcomes: Opintojakson käytyään: - Opiskelija tunnistaa jakelukanaviin liittyvät toiminnot, virrat ja prosessit sekä pystyy määrittämään jakelun tavoitteet logistiikan ja kaupan liiketoiminnan näkökulmasta. -Opiskelija osaa arvioida kaupan liiketoimintamalleja sekä ymmärtää kaupan ja logistiikan taloudellisen ja yhteiskunnallisen -Opiskelija tunnistaa jakelutoimintojen keskinäisiä vuorovaikutuksia ja pystyy analysoimaan niiden vaikutuksia yrityksen toimintaan.
content: - Opintojaksolla tarkastellaan jakelukanavien rakenteellisia, toiminnallisia ja sosiaalisia tekijöitä ja toimintamalleja. -Tutustutaan logistisiin toimintoihin, niiden koordinointiin, kanavajäsenten rooleihin ja tehtäviin sekä kaupan toimintamalleihin (esim. franchising, osuuskunnat, e-kauppa, monikanavainen jakelu). -Jakelukanavien toimintojen vuorovaikutuksia ja suunnittelutehtäviä tarkastellaan myös havainnollistavien laskennallisten esimerkkien avulla.
prerequisites: Suositellaan: Markkinoinnin perusteet. Mikäli opintojaksolle ilmoittautuneiden lukumäärä ylittää maksimin, voidaan etusijalle asettaa ne, joilla on markkinoinnin perusteet suoritettuna.
learningMaterial: Luennoitsijan määrittelemät artikkelit ja muu opintomateriaali.
workload: Verkkototeutus Moodlessa. Ryhmätyö ja Exam-tentti. Harjoitustehtävät sekä luento- ja kirjallisuuskuulustelu on suoritettava hyväksytysti saman kalenterivuoden aikana.

name: Brand Experience in Retailing
learningOutcomes: After completing the course, the student has an understanding of the value of branding and creating superior brand experiences as part of today's retail management. The student can identify the variety of touchpoints that customers have with the brand over their customer journey. Furthermore, the student is able to develop and plan these touchpoints to enable superior customer experiences.
content: The course familiarizes students with the role of brand management and the power of creating superior brand experiences in today's competitive, global retail environment. The course introduces key concepts of retail brand experience including retail brand strategy, experience dimensions, customer journeys and brand touchpoints, brand communication, brand loyalty and brand co-creation. The course gives students insights on how to build attractive, omnichannel brand concepts and how to co-create retail brands that resonate with customers.
prerequisites: Recommended: Basics in marketing.
workload: 9 themes. Videolectures given by professors and business visitors for each theme. Curation of other relevant videos from Youtube. Scientific articles. Assignments (1-4). Exam in Moodle.

name: Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems
learningOutcomes: After the course, the student is able to analytically solve and analyze simple ordinary differential equations equations. Student is able to solve ordinary differential equations and systems and basic partial differential equations numerically, using Matlab solvers. Student is able to model engineering problems as differential equations.
content: Linear and nonlinear ordinary differential equations revised. Initial and boundary value problems. Stability and phase space presentation of solutions. Asymptotical analysis. Approximative and numerical solutions for ordinary differential equations with series method and Matlab solvers. Introduction to partial differential equations: advection, diffusion/heat, wave equations. Numerical solutions with semidiscretization methods. Modelling examples from different engineering fields.
prerequisites: BM20A6800 Matematiikka II, osa B or similar basic knowledge of differential equations.
learningMaterial: Lecture material available in Moodle
workload: Completion method 1: exam. 3rd period: lectures 28 h, exercises 21 h, and independent practice 30 h. 4th period: lectures 28 h, exercises 21 h, independent practice 31 h, and exam 3 h. Total 162 h.

name: Biorefinery Process Development Project
learningOutcomes: After completing the course the student understands the complex connections between biorefinery feedstocks, process technology, and product quality. The student can apply their knowledge to react e.g. in case of varying feed quality, process failures or changes in product specifications.
content: This is the capstone course in Biorefineries Master's programme. Previously acquired knowledge on biorefinery feedstocks, conversion methods, separation and purification methods, as well as products and markets are applied to study a complete biorefinery process.
prerequisites: Recommended prerequisites courses are highly recommended before participating in BPDP.
learningMaterial: To be announced in Moodle.
workload: Lectures, seminars and tutoring meetings 20h, development project in groups and reporting 250 h. Total workload 270 h.
equivalentCoursesInfo: Starting from 2021-22, this course replaces BJ02A1081 Research Project Course, 10 ECTS in the MSc in Biorefineries.

name: Laser Based Manufacturing for Design
learningOutcomes: After having passed the course, the student will: - understand how laser beams and systems are used in materials processing - realize how these processes can be utilized to full in product development of a company - be able to compare and generalize the special features gained with creative use of different laser based processes and the impact and utilization of the special features of these processes on product design - understand what kind of properties can be gained with use of laser based processes and how does this effect on design flow of a product - understand how the real total cost analysis and sustainability studies can be carried out and how they compete with conventional manufacturing technologies - Realizes what kind of quality can be reached and how these technologies can be used for increasing energy efficiency and save material. - have design skills that are needed to reform technological readiness in different industries - have understanding of laser based manufacturing solutions for advanced energy sector industry in the future
content: The possibilities and limitations of laser processing on the product design. The utilization of laser based processes into design routines and philosophies, together with mechanical properties in comparison with conventional manufacturing technologies. Practical case examples. Economic aspects of laser materials processing. The features of most common laser based processes i.e. various different versions and applications of e.g. laser marking, cutting, welding and surface treatment processes. In addition, design aspects of a laser based additive manufacturing technology ( e.g. 3D metal printing) is covered.
prerequisites: Course BK30A1201 Laser Materials Processing passed.
learningMaterial: Course material in Moodle.
evaluationCriteria: Grade 0-5, written report 80 %, seminar 20 %.
workload: Lectures 12 h. Guided group working in teams (5x2h), 10 h. Design, execution and reporting of project work in teams 113 h. Total workload 135 h.The course is suitable for distance learning.

name: Physics of Semiconductor Devices
learningOutcomes: Student will acquire an in-depth knowledge of the most important semiconductor components and their operation principle.
content: Structure, operation and physics of semiconductor devices.
learningMaterial: Sze, Physics of Semiconductor Devices.
evaluationCriteria: 0-5, 30% home exercises, 30% exam, 40% special assignment.
workload: Lectures 20 h, home exercises 50 h, special assignment 62 h, preparation to exam 30 h. Total workload 162 h.

name: Work Experience in Master's Degree
learningOutcomes: After the module a student - has become acquainted with an industrial working environment in the field of chemical or process industry - has obtained experience in practical application of his/her knowledge and skills - has seen operation of production processes and equipment of his field in practice - can analyze the practical role of knowledge and skills he/she has learned in his/her studies.
content: Practical operating, research, design or quality control work in chemical or process industry, laboratory or engineering company. Work period must be 4 weeks full time or corresponding amount of working hours (150) as minimum. Master's thesis work can not be approved as work experience. Company collaboration Work experience period is done in a company, research center or university.
evaluationCriteria: Pass/Fail, report 100%.
workload: Work experience approval can be applied after practical employment of 4–7 weeks. Uploading the filled application and report (both forms are available in eLUT) and copy of the work certificate to a Moodle platform ‘Kemiantekniikan työkokemus/Work experience in Chemical Engineering’ is requested. Four weeks employment is required to complete 2 ECTS of work experience. Total workload of 2 ECTS (54 hours) consists of: Applying for a job and recruiting 10 h, Tasks connected to beginning of employment (e.g. orientation, rules of the employment and workplace) 15 h, Observing (while working) how the working community operates (e.g. how work/production is organized, supervision, working manners of the working community, social environment of the workplace) 24 h, Writing a report 5 h (2-3 pages). A student can apply altogether 3-10 ECTS of work experience by taking additional tasks related to study field worth 27-216 h. Extra ECTS can be added to free elective studies as a study draft.

name: Digital Electronics
learningOutcomes: After the completion of course, the student is able to design, implement and simulate digital systems based on sequential logic. He/she is able to describe the functionality and implementation of basic sequential logic circuits, registries, memories, programmable logic circuits. In addition, the student is able to understand how digital systems are implemented with electronics and what physical limitations are involved.
content: Sequential logic, components based on sequential logic, registries, memories, programmable logic circuits, design, simulation and implementation of digital systems, design of algorithmic state machines.
prerequisites: BL40A1730 Digitaalitekniikka (Digital technology)Basics of digital technology (Boolean algebra, combinatorial logic systems)
learningMaterial: Lecture material in Moodle. Additionally, it is recommended to follow the book Floyd, Digital Fundamentals to the appropriate extent.Additional book/material M. Morris Mano, Digital Design.
evaluationCriteria: 0-5 (Moodle exam) + 70 % of home work assignments accepted to pass the course. Extra points from home assignments valid for three (3) following Moodle exams (max. 15 points/exam)
workload: Lectures 18 h, exercises 12 h, individual weekly assignments. Independent work 51 h, 2nd period.Moodle examination and weekly quizzes. On line course. Total workload 81 h.

name: Digital Signal Processing II
learningOutcomes: Upon completion of the course the student will be able to: 1. describe the practical implementation of digital filters, 2. describe the finite word length effects on the frequency response and operation of a filter, 3. in order to minimize these effects, transform the direct-form implementations into a more beneficial format with respect to the finite word length effects and do the required scaling, 4. describe the representations of fixed and floating point numbers, 5. design FIR and IIR filters with the ready-made software and describe the basics of design methods, 6. know applications of optimal and adaptive filters, 7. implement median filters.
content: The finite word length effects and elimination of these effects. Alternative structures for discrete-time systems and their programming implementation. Computer-aided design of digital filters. Decimation and interpolation. Median filters. Optimal and adaptive filters.
prerequisites: BL40A0401 Signaalien digitaalinen käsittely I (Digital Signal Processing I) or corresponding knowledge.
learningMaterial: Proakis, J.G.and Manolakis, D.G.: Digital Signal Processing, Principles,Algorithms, and Applications. Lecture slides. Luukko, J.: Digitaalinen suodatus (luentomoniste)
evaluationCriteria: Examination 60% (max. 60 p.), assignment 40% (max. 40 p.).
workload: 14 h of lectures and 14 h of tutorials, 1st period. 14 h of lectures, 14 h of tutorials, 30 h of assignment with seminar, 2nd period. Written examination in Moodle. Independent study 22 h. Total workload 108 h. Applicable for distance students.

name: Digital Water
learningOutcomes: The aim of the course is to introduce a chemical engineering professional with the multiple opportunities of digitalization in the water treatment sector. After completing the course, the student · Will have identified his/her own skill gap in applying digitalization in the water treatment sector · Will have developed domain-specific knowledge on the possibilities of digitalization to further innovate in his/her domain
content: The course will cover current and relevant topics in digitalization of the water treatment sector. The course is an entry-level introductory course supporting life-long learning.
evaluationCriteria: Pass / Fail
workload: Online lectures and interview clips 10 h, self-study 29 h, self-guided exercises 15 h. Total workload 54 h.

name: Digital Design
learningOutcomes: The course is an introduction to digital design and digital electronics. Upon completion of the course the student will be able to analyse and design simple digital systems by using Boolean algebra and elementary components based on it.
content: The digital presentation of information, binary numbers, Boolean algebra, combinatorial logic and elementary components based on it, the analysis, design and simulation of digital circuits based on combinatorial logic, flip-flops, the analysis of sequential logic.
learningMaterial: Floyd: Digital Fundamentals, lecture material and lecture notes.
evaluationCriteria: 0-5, examination 100 %. In addition, at least 70 % of maximum home exercise points are required to pass the course.
workload: Lectures 18 h, exercises 12 h, individual assignments 45 h, exam 3 h. Total workload 78 h.

name: Work Internship in Master's Degree
learningOutcomes: After the work environment internship, the student has obtained a basic knowledge of the work, work environment and working community in his/her own field. The student is able to apply and generalize knowledge and skills acquired during the course of studies to work in his/her own field.
content: The student obtains a (summer) job from the company, works as a paid employee, requests a certificate of employment and applies for the approval of the work as an internship for the Master’s degree. Full-time employment relationships of at least four weeks can be approved as internships. The completion of the Master’s thesis is not accepted as an internship. An employment relationship that took place before the studies can be approved as an internship providing that it has not been accepted and included in any other previous degree.

name: Work experience in Master's degree in Finland
learningOutcomes: After the work experience, the student will have the basic knowledge of work, working environment and working community in the field of the studies. The student will be able to apply the knowledge and skills acquired during the course of studies to work in their own field. Completion of the course supports the development of the following generic competences for working life: Know-how on own field, developing own skills in working life, career management aspects.
content: The student obtains a (summer) job in a company, works there as a paid employee, requests for a certificate of employment and applies for the approval of the work experience for the Master's degree. Full-time employment relationships of at least four weeks can be approved as work experience. The completion of the Master's thesis is not accepted as work experience. An employment relationship preceding the studies can be approved, provided that it has not been accepted and included in any other previous degree.
learningMaterial: Instructions and application and report forms in eLUT portal: https://elut.lut.fi/en/completing-studies/work-internships
evaluationCriteria: Pass/Fail. Report 100 %.
workload: Practical work experience of min. of 4 weeks. Written report including a description of working environment, tasks of the student and their contribution to the goals and operation of the company. First 2 ECTS credits: applying for a job and recruiting 10 h, tasks connected to starting an employment relationship 15 h, observing (while working) how the working community operates 24 h, a written report 5 h (2-3 papers), total 54 h. Next 1-4 ECTS credits: having different tasks in a company 27-108 h. (1 ECTS credit/27 h). Total workload 54-162 h. Work experience can be added to the free elective studies of the Bachelor's degree.

name: Introduction to distance learning
learningOutcomes: Students will become familiar with mechanical engineering degree program and university studies as well as distance program's requirements. Students are able to design their studies and track their progress according to their own goals. Students will become familiar with the Lappeenranta Academic Library as well as learn the basics of information retrieval. Students get familiar with information security in university and make an Moodle exam about reporting instructions.
content: After the course the student is able to describe the general structure of Master's degree study in mechanical engineering. Student understands the different stages of their studies as well as the meaning of Personal Study Plan. Students are able to look for advice related to their studies and is familiar with reporting instructions of their own department. Students recognize the services offered by the library and knows the mechanical engineering related information can be found from library's data base. The student knows the distance-program, various services and used tools.
learningMaterial: Material available in Moodle.
evaluationCriteria: Pass/Fail. Tiedonhaun perusteet course pass. Personal Study Plan pass. Information security-exercise. Reporting-exam pass. Completion of the Study Skills section.
workload: Lectures 6h, 1st period. Independent study 48h. Total workload for student 52 h. The course is suitable for distance learning.

name: Introduction to Digital Learning of Electrical Engineering
learningOutcomes: Upon completion of the course the student will be able to 1. describe the general structure and composition of his/her degree programme, 2. prepare a personal study plan (ePSP) and schedule his/her studies, 3. use the services of the university library and conduct independent information searches, 4. know how to improve information security during his/her daily use of university networks, 5. identify the student services and search for the advising personnel and material related to their studies.
content: Introduction to study structures of digital degree programmes in Electrical Engineering. Preparing a personal study plan (ePSP). Getting to know the library and its services. Basics of scientific information retrieval. Concern oneself with information security in daily life.
learningMaterial: Material available in Moodle.
evaluationCriteria: Pass/Fail. Satisfactorily completed learning assignments and online courses of Information searching and Information security training. Preparing Personal Study Plan.
workload: Video lectures. Preparing personal study plan. Discussion with a teacher tutor. Learning assignments. Online courses Information searching and Information security training. 1st and 2nd periods. Total workload 54 h.

name: Design of Steel Structures
learningOutcomes: After completing the course students can design welded structures for demanding applications, considering also fabrication requirements, which means they can: - recognize the essential design criteria, - define the design loading for the structure and recognize the joint types based on the loading of joint - define the deformations and stresses due to welding and eliminate them purposefully - calculate the required throat thickness for weld - analyze the stress concentrations of welded joints and choose the most purposeful method for fatigue design - design plate structures (welded and cold formed) considering stability - design the structures and joints by using plastic limit state method - evaluate the risk of brittle fracture by using numerical methods, especially in case of arctic structures - design beams considering also torsion, warping, distortion, shear lag, etc. - optimize structures, especially considering the potential of high and ultra high strength steels - design bolted connections
content: During the course the students get familiar with the following: Failure criteria, definition of joint types and analyzing variable amplitude loading. Background for distortions due to welding, evaluation methods and minimization of consequences. Theoretical background for design of fillet welds. Analyzing stress concentrations according to local approaches and the most common fatigue design methods (Nominal, Hot spot, ENS, Local Strain and LEFM). Theoretical background and design (EC3) for buckling of plates, columns and beams. Plasticity theory of beams, frames and plates (yield line method). Numerical methods for analyzing brittle fracture considering the material properties of welded joints. Theory of thin walled structures. Practical approach for design and multi-objective optimization on welded structures considering the global and local structural behavior and fabrication of details and the potential of high strength materials. Failure modes of bolded joints
prerequisites: Basic mathematics (solving equations, derivation and integration). Completed studies of Statics and Strength of materials.
learningMaterial: Handout and the supporting material (see reference list of handout).
evaluationCriteria: Examination 60 % and home-calculations 40 %.
workload: Homeworks 70 h. Individual work 80 h. Laboratory work, including demonstrations and practical tasks of strength of welded components and joints 10 h. Total 160 h. The course is suitable for distance learning.

name: Design for Manufacturing
learningOutcomes: Students are able to Understand how manufacturing methods and material selection might affect the design process. Describe manufacturing processes considering designed applications, users and economic impacts Define and differentiate diverse manufacturing processes in mass production of products Understand and explain effect of material selection in production process of a concept Define the key function of production tools on final product features Highlight key production prerequisites in transformation of design to a final product balancing aesthetic and functionality
content: Multi-disciplinary problem solving approach Manufacturing processes in a production environment context Conducting research in design Functional and technical requirements from engineering perspectives Product design process based on the perceptual understanding from manufacturing perspective Manufacturing technologies, technical production parameters and material selection Design methodology and product development

name: Design of Experiments
learningOutcomes: After the course, the student is expected to master the basic skills for effective experimentation, and regression analysis and basic analyses of variance (ANOVA): - understanding of the importance of designed experiments - ability to apply the basic experimental plans, and regression techniques to analyse the results - skills to optimize an engineering process using design of experiments and data analysis.
content: Importance of experimental design, minimization of prediction uncertainty of regression models. Basic factorial designs: 2N, Central Composite designs for regression analysis. Screening designs. Response surfaces. Experimental optimisation and uncertainty estimation.
prerequisites: First year university calculus, BM20A1401 Tilastomatematiikka I/basic statistics. Basic (Matlab) skills for technical computing with PC.
learningMaterial: Box, G., Hunter, S., Hunter, W. G.: Statistics for Experimenters, Wiley 2005, 2nd Edition. Montgomery, D. C.: Design and Analysis of Experiments, Wiley 2013, 8th Edition. Lecture notes
evaluationCriteria: 0-5, workshops 30 %, assignments 40 %, project work 30 %.
workload: Lectures and seminar 7 h, workshops 6 h, home assignments 35 h, experimental work, modelling and reporting 40 h, independent study 20 h, 4th period. Total 108 h.

name: Design of Fluid Machinery
learningOutcomes: By the end of the course, students will be able to 1. do the aerodynamic design of axial and radial flow turbines and radial compressors, 2. understand the design principles of axial and radial flow turbines and radial compressors, 3. understand the differences of bearing types, basic's of the rotor dynamics and balancing of rotating machines, 4. understand the operating principle of a gas turbine, and 5. describe the measurement setup of a jet engine and analyze the measured data. Completion of the course supports the development of the following generic competences for working life: know-how on own field, knowledge of the research of own field, practical application of theories, working independently, problem solving, information retrieval, critical thinking skills, analytical thinking skills.
content: Compressor design, turbine design, bearings, rotor dynamics, balancing of rotating machines, gas turbine measurement.
learningMaterial: Lecture material in Moodle.
evaluationCriteria: numerical assessment (0-5), homeworks 20%, exercises 50%, laboratory work 30%
workload: 3rd period: 8 h lectures, 6 h exercises, 66 h independent work. 4th period: 2 h lectures, 2 h exercises, 29 h laboratory work, 22 h independent work. Total workload 135 h.

name: Digital Twins as a part of data pipeline
learningOutcomes: Student is able to - identify digital twin operation principles and application areas - identify game-like activities and possibilities in the digital twin operational environment - identify game engine possibilities in the digital twins' presentation layer - implement simple digital twin using modern game engine

learningMaterial: Details available in Completion methods under the header Teaching

name: District Heating
learningOutcomes: Upon completion of the course the student will be able to 1. describe the basics of district heating in the world and in Finland, 2. explain the technical solutions of generating and delivering district heating at a detailed level, do engineering design to 3. dimension heat output and annual thermal energy necessary for various heating applications, 4. understand and calculate various losses, 5. evaluate the basic design and use of district heating networks and heat production.
content: The formation of energy demand in buildings and the consumption variation. Consumer devices, connections and energy measurement. Abitility to calculate piping losses, and understand principles of piping and network planning and control. Production of district heating, district heating plants and heating power plants.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of heat transfer, fluid dynamics and power plant engineering recommended
learningMaterial: Lecture notes.
evaluationCriteria: 0 - 5. Written assignment, weekly tasks
workload: 3rd period: 12 h of lectures. Independent study 12 h. Independent calculations and online tasks 20 h. 4th period: Written assignment 48 h. Peer evaluation 16 h. Total workload 108 h.

name: Work experience in Master's degree in Finland
learningOutcomes: After the work experience, the student will have the basic knowledge of work, working environment and working community in the field of the studies. The student will be able to apply the knowledge and skills acquired during the course of studies to work in their own field. Completion of the course supports the development of the following generic competences for working life: Know-how on own field, developing own skills in working life, career management aspects.
content: The student obtains a (summer) job in a company, works there as a paid employee, requests for a certificate of employment and applies for the approval of the work experience for the Master's degree. Full-time employment relationships of at least four weeks can be approved as work experience. The completion of the Master's thesis is not accepted as work experience. An employment relationship preceding the studies can be approved, provided that it has not been accepted and included in any other previous degree.
learningMaterial: Instructions and application and report forms in eLUT portal: https://elut.lut.fi/en/completing-studies/work-internships
evaluationCriteria: Pass/Fail. Report 100 %.
workload: Practical work experience of a min. of 4 weeks. Written report including a description of working environment, tasks of the student and their contribution to the goals and operation of the company. First 2 ECTS credits: applying for a job and recruiting 10 h, tasks connected to starting an employment relationship 15 h, observing (while working) how the working community operates 24 h, a written report 5 h (2-3 papers), total 54 h. Next 1-4E CTS credits: having different tasks in a company 27-108 h. (1 ECTS credit/27 h). Total workload 54-162 h. Students can add work experience to free elective studies.

name: Work Experience in Master's degree in Finland
learningOutcomes: After the work internship, the student will be able to define and explain what is involved in working for an employer in his/her own field and what the basic rules of the world of work are from the employee's perspective, and further, how to act in a working community.
content: Applying for a job and recruiting, tasks connected to starting an employment relationship (e.g. orientation, the rules of the employment relationship and the work place), observing (while working) how the working community operates (e.g. how work/production is organised, supervision, the working manners of the working community/teams, the social environment of the work place), practical working in a company.
evaluationCriteria: Pass/Fail, report 100%.
workload: Practical work experience of a min. of 4 weeks. Written report including a description of working environment, tasks of the student and their contribution to the goals and operation of the company. name: Electrical Drives
learningOutcomes: Upon completion of the course the student will be able to: 1. understand the role of electrical drives, 2. understand different torque producing principles in different machines, 3. model and simulate a DC motor drive, 4. describe the principles of scalar, vector and direct torque control of rotating field machines, 5. define and understand the functioning of the most important power electronic converters, 6. discuss the principles of PWM in general, space vector modulation and DTC, 7. model the behaviour of permanent magnet synchronous machine by using vector equivalent circuits and vector diagrams, 8. understand synchronous machine control in details, 9. understand synchronous reluctance machine control in details, 10. understand the role of induction machine and its control in details, 11. know the switched reluctance machine control principles, 12. discuss the adverse effects of PWM systems on motor behaviour and the wave nature of the motor cable. Mastering the course material well gives the student comprehensive understanding of the basics of electrical drives and wide possibilities to work in the field. This is the course for drives professionals.
content: Theory of electric motor drives, operation and vector equivalent circuits. Synchronous machine drives, asynchronous machine drives, synchronous reluctance machine drives, permanent magnet synchronous machine drives, switched reluctance motor drives. Torque production in different machines. Power electronic converters suitable for motor and generator drives. Scalar control, vector control, direct flux linkage control and direct torque control (DTC). Motor cable wave nature, bearing currents. Applying the principles for practical electrical machine types.
evaluationCriteria: 0-5. Independent homework 60 % and written Moodle examination 40 %.
workload: Lectures 24 h, tutorials 24 h, 2nd period. Lectures 24 h, tutorials 24 h, 3rd period. Independent study including homework tasks 117 h. Moodle examination 3 h. Total workload 216 h.
equivalentCoursesInfo: BL30A1040 Electrical Drives 1 (4 ECTS) + BL30A1050 Electrical Drives 2 (4 ECTS) will together replace this Electrical Drives (8 ECTS).

name: Ergonomics in Design
learningOutcomes: · Describe and explain basic ergonomic methods and theories in relation to the products and services · Identify and explain different characteristics of physical, cognitive and organizational human abilities and restrictions · Identify harmful conditions in the work environment and recommendations for improvements · Explain the role of ergonomic design in the daily life of people with restrictions and disabilities · Apply their knowledge in ergonomic theories in the development stage of products and environments · Summarize and demonstrate the result of an ergonomic study on a real case study · Analyze ergonomic characteristics through empirical and theoretical investigations and apply them in improved proposal/design

name: Machine Dynamics
learningOutcomes: The student will learn theories and practices of structural dynamics and knows how to apply the knowledge in the design of machine systems. He/she is able to model dynamic machine systems, solve the equations of motion in frequency and time domains and analyze the results from simulations and measurements. The student knows the basics of vibrations measurements and experimental modal analysis. The student is able to review and interpret his/her student mate's simulation results resembling the tasks in the later career. Some of the practical examples and assignments are real-life cases arising from co-operation with industrial companies.
content: Multiple degree-of-freedom vibrations, solution and interpretation of natural frequencies and modes. Response to the harmonic and general force excitation. Derivation of the equations of motion of the system and solution in the frequency and time domain. Vibration measurements and experimental modal analysis. Introduction to rotor dynamics. Torsional vibrations.
prerequisites: Students are recommended to have basic skills on Dynamics. Experience or basic studies of Finite Element Method (FEM) is also recommend, but not required.
learningMaterial: Lecture notes.
evaluationCriteria: 0-5, online examination or online mid-term examinations 50 %, homework and laboratory exercises 50 %.

name: Nuclear Reactor Design
searchTags: Written examination in the examination schedule
learningOutcomes: Upon completion of the course the students will be able to explain physical phenomena underlying nuclear reactors, and perform engineering design of a critical nuclear reactor using diffusion theory, and perform thermal engineering design of the reactor core. Students will learn the main characteristics of commercially important nuclear reactor types. Completion of the course supports the development of the following generic competences for working life: Know-how on own field, Written communication, Oral communication, Team working skills, Problem solving, Information retrieval, Time management and prioritizing tasks.
content: Interaction of radiation with matter. Nuclear reactions and their cross sections. Reactor physics, diffusion theory, a simplified criticality calculation. The design principles for the reactor core, thermal dimensioning. Major commercial nuclear reactor types: PWR, BWR, Small Modular Reactors, CANDU and RBMK, gas-cooled reactors, and fast reactors.
prerequisites: BH30A0001 Introduction to Nuclear Energy, or BH30A0020 Introduction to Nuclear Power Engineering, or equivalent skills.
learningMaterial: Lecture notes. Lamarsh & Baratta: Introduction to Nuclear Engineering, 3rd edition (2014), where applicable.
evaluationCriteria: 0-5. Written examination 70 %, assignment and seminar presentation 30 %.
workload: Completion method 1. Exam: Lectures 28 h, tutorials 14 h, assignment 42 h, 1st period. Lectures 14 h, tutorials 14 h, seminar presentation 20 h, preparation for the exam 27 h and exam 3 h, 2nd period. Total workload 162 h.

name: Nuclear Reactor Dynamics

learningOutcomes: Upon completion of the course the student will be able to explain nuclear reactor kinetics and related feedback mechanisms, principles of nuclear reactor control, and principles of efficient nuclear fuel utilisation. Completion of the course supports the development of the following generic competences for working life: know-how on own field, mathematics and natural sciences, practical application of theories, problem solving.
content: Nuclear reactor kinetics, reactivity feedbacks in critical reactors. Nuclear reactor dynamic response and control. Neutron sources, approach to criticality, reactivity excursions, reactor power management, reactor poisons, fuel burnup management.

learningMaterial: Lecture notes. Reuss: Neutron Physics, Part I, as applicable. Lamarsh ; Baratta: Introduction to Nuclear Engineering, as applicable.

name: Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations
learningOutcomes: How partial differential equations (PDEs) are used in science and technology and how solutions to elliptic and parabolic PDEs can be approximated with the finite element method. Basics of Sobolev spaces, weak solutions to PDEs, and error analysis of the finite element method. After the course students are able to implement a 2D finite element solver and are familiar with finite element software.
content: The diffusion–advection–reaction equation is a partial differential equation (PDE) that describes a wide variety of phenomena in science and technology, such as transport phenomena in fluid flows. The course covers the basic theory of such elliptic and parabolic PDEs and their numerical solution using the finite element method (FEM). Theoretical topics include basics weak derivatives, Sobolev spaces, weak solutions to PDEs, existence and uniqueness of weak solutions, and error analysis of FEM. The methodological part of the course focuses on piecewise linear FEM and its implementation in 2D for Poisson's equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions. The course also contains an introduction to finite element software (e.g., Elmer).
prerequisites: Bachelor level studies in mathematics. BM20A7300 Functional analysis or an equivalent course is recommended.
learningMaterial: Lecture notes and the books - Knabner & Angerman. Numerical Methods for Elliptic and Parabolic Partial Differential Equations: With contributions by Andreas Rupp. 2nd ed. Springer, 2021. doi: 10.1007/978-3-030-79385-2 - Kuzmin & Hämäläinen. Finite Element Methods for Computational Fluid Dynamics: A Practical Guide. SIAM, 2024. https://doi.org/10.1137/1.9781611973617
evaluationCriteria: 0-5, EXAM-examination 100%
workload: Lectures 14h, Exercises 14h, Independent study and preparation for exam 107h. Total 135h

name: Power Plant Design
searchTags: Written examination in the examination schedule
learningOutcomes: Upon completion of the course the students will be able to 1. explain the advanced processes of thermal power plants (excl. nuclear energy), 2. describe the methods used for the reduction of emissions related to energy production, 3. estimate the impact of power plant control on the utilization economy and usability, 4. apply thermodynamics and mass and energy balances to improve the efficiency and the operation of the energy processes, 5. design power plant processes for the production of electricity and heat and select the appropriate auxiliary equipment, and 6. describe the phases in the implementation of power plant projects. Completion of the course supports the development of the following generic competences for working life: mathematics and natural sciences, practical application of theories, working independently, problem solving, and time management and prioritizing tasks.
content: Special features of different power plant types. Engineering design: planning and design of power plants and distributed energy systems, simulation and modelling. Implementation of power plant projects. Utilisation and control of power plants, emission reduction. Future energy systems.
prerequisites: BH50A0200 Introduction to Power Plant Engineering attended.
learningMaterial: Lecture notes.
evaluationCriteria: 0 - 5. Examination, planning assignment, continuous evaluation.
workload: 1st period: 18 h of lectures, 18 h of tutorials. 2nd period: Planning assignment as team work. Written examination. Independent study approximately: Planning assignment 49 h. Preparation for the examination 24 h and the examination 3 h. Studying given material 50 h. Total workload 162 h.

name: Reliability Based Machine Element Design
learningOutcomes: After successfully completing this course, the student will be able to: - utilize different reliability based measures for machine element design as well as manufacturing - apply tools and techniques for risk analysis of a machine or mechanical system - compare materials and manufacturing processes for reliable machine elements - use principles, with which the designer can improve the product to reduce the failure probability - apply failure mode analysis, especially in context of wear and corrosion phenomena - choose an appropriate distribution to analyze reliability aspects of a component
content: The course will cover the following topics: - The importance of multidisciplinary optimization including reliability based constraints in design is discussed - Tools and techniques for both qualitative and quantitative risk analysis of an assembly or a technical system are presented. - Aspects, how uncertainties associated with statistical distributions and any insufficient information may lead to large errors in probability calculations in engineering are clarified. - Analytical tools for analyzing failure modes of machine elements, machines and technical systems are taught. - Guidelines to choose an appropriate distribution to analyze reliability aspects and lifetime of a component are presented.
prerequisites: B.Sc. (Mech.Eng.) Degree or equivalent knowledge.
learningMaterial: Lecture notes and other learning materials to be provided during the course on Moodle Birolini, Alessandro. Reliability engineering. Vol. 5. Berlin: Springer, 2007.
evaluationCriteria: 0-5, 4 group exercises (in total 70%, instructions of exercises will be given together with lectures), final presentation (30%, mandatory attendance in campus for Everyone, in addition to giving presentation, each group is expected to listen to at least 3 presentations)
workload: Lectures 10h, presentation 1h, exercise in class 10h, groupwork 114 h, total workload 135 h. Lappeenranta students and Lahti students have different schedules. As for contact teaching degree programme, students must present both lecture and exercises in classroom.

content: - Discussion about real life challenges, companies had during product and brand development stage - Organization orientations in product development - Design philosophy, knowledge and skills of different industrial designers - Various contexts surrounding the product design and development - Cross-disciplinary collaboration in product development - New product development and commercialization challenges- internal and external considerations - Evaluation of strategic and economic potential in product development - Design contribution in economic success of a firm - Role of designers and their affect in society in context of the Interaction between design, culture and society
